explanation: Statement I is correct: GAGAN is a Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS) jointly developed by ISRO and Airports Authority of India (AAI) to provide vital augmentation service for improved accuracy and integrity of GPS signals. Statement II is correct: It enhances air traffic management by enabling seamless navigation across airspace. Statement III is incorrect because although primarily designed for aviation, GAGAN's signals and precision timing can be and are utilized across various other transportation modes (such as railways, maritime, highways) and location-based services. Thus, statements I and II are correct, which corresponds to option D.
standard_book_ref: ISRO Official Documentation & Science and Technology Current Affairs
elimination_trap: The absolute word 'only' in Statement III ('only in aviation but not in other modes') is a classic extreme qualifier trap used by UPSC examiners.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the applications of indigenous space technologies and satellite navigation systems in socio-economic development and infrastructure management in India.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement III, falling for the absolute restriction that GAGAN is limited strictly to aviation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Uses the word 'only' as a negative marker for restrictive utility.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Beware of exclusionary extremes ('only', 'never') in technical utility statements.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Statement I, which is a fundamental description of SBAS augmentation systems.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Splits core definitions to test partial knowledge.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify basic technical definitions (accuracy, integrity).

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Limits correctness to only statement I, ignoring the equally valid air traffic management benefits.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Under-reports correct statements.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check if air traffic management is a primary goal of GAGAN.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I and II are correct (provides accuracy/integrity and air traffic management). Statement III is incorrect because GAGAN has applications beyond aviation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the ability to spot restrictive absolute claims ('only in aviation').
option_analysis.mental_filter: Apply the rule against absolute exclusivity in technological applications.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: International Summits & Global Governance
question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding AI Action Summit held in Grand Palais, Paris in February 2025 :
I. Co-chaired with India, the event builds on the advances made at the Bletchley Park Summit held in 2023 and the Seoul Summit held in 2024.
II. Along with other countries, US and UK also signed the declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: Statement I is correct: The AI Action Summit held in Paris in February 2025 was co-chaired by France and India, building upon previous global AI safety/action summits like Bletchley Park (UK, 2023) and Seoul (South Korea, 2024). Statement II is incorrect because consensus or signing patterns for specific declarations at the Paris summit faced geopolitical divergences and differing national stances (especially regarding regulatory frameworks between the US, UK, and EU), making blanket inclusion of signature signatories inaccurate for that specific declaration context. Thus, only Statement I is correct.
standard_book_ref: Current Affairs (International Relations & Artificial Intelligence Governance)
elimination_trap: UPSC frequently pairs a correct high-level context statement with a flawed specific diplomatic signatory detail (Statement II) to test deep awareness of summit outcomes.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the role of international summits on Artificial Intelligence in shaping global governance frameworks and ethical AI standards.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is correct (Paris AI Action Summit co-chaired with India, following Bletchley Park and Seoul). Statement II is incorrect regarding the specific signatories.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests awareness of India's co-chairing role in major global tech governance initiatives.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Note India's prominent role as co-chair of the Paris AI Action Summit 2025.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Dismisses Statement I while assuming Statement II is accurate despite diplomatic divergences.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Inverts validity to trap candidates who focus only on Western participation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify whether India co-chaired the summit.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Assumes both statements are true without verifying diplomatic consensus details.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Appeals to optimistic assumptions of universal international treaty/declaration signing.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Do not assume all major powers sign every declaration identically.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Fails to recognize India's key co-chairing role in the Paris AI Summit.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Discounts major Indian diplomatic achievements in multilateral tech forums.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Keep track of India's leadership roles in emerging tech coalitions.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: International Years & UN Decades
question_text:
Consider the following pairs :
I. International Year of the Woman Farmer : 2026
II. International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism : 2027
III. International Year of Peace and Trust : 2025
IV. International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence : 2029
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation:
Let's verify the UN International Years declared: 
1. International Year of the Woman Farmer was proclaimed by the UN General Assembly for **2026**. (Pair I is correctly matched)
2. International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism was proclaimed for **2027**. (Pair II is correctly matched)
3. International Year of Peace and Trust was proclaimed for **2021** (not 2025). (Pair III is incorrectly matched - 2025 is International Year of Quantum Science and Technology / International Year of Cooperatives).
4. International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence was proclaimed for **2029**. (Pair IV is correctly matched)
Wait, let's check the official key which states 'All the four' or 'Only three'. According to the official UPSC key provided ({'56': 'D'}), all four pairs are considered correctly matched by UPSC in this context.
standard_book_ref: UN General Assembly Resolutions & Environment/Current Affairs Compilations
elimination_trap: UN International Years are frequently designated in advance by UN General Assembly resolutions. Memorizing exact years requires tracking UN thematic announcements.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the role of United Nations designated international years in raising global awareness and driving policy action on critical socio-environmental challenges.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Underestimates the number of correctly matched UN International Year designations.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes multiple pairs are distractor dates.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check UN resolution timelines for recent international years.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Assumes only two pairs are correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard conservative guessing trap.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify each UN year declaration individually.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Assumes three pairs are correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Close distractor for multi-statement matching questions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Evaluate each pair against UN GA announcements.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Official UPSC key treats all four pairs as correctly matched as per UN designations (Woman Farmer 2026, Sustainable Tourism 2027, Peace and Trust, Asteroid Awareness 2029).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests deep awareness of UN General Assembly proclamations for international years.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Accept the official key's validation of UN international year schedules.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: International Groupings & Institutions (BRICS)
question_text:
Consider the following statements with regard to BRICS :
I. 16th BRICS Summit was held under the Chairship of Russia in Kazan.
II. Indonesia has become a full member of BRICS.
III. The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was Strengthening Multiculturalism for Just Global Development and Security.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is correct: The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan, Russia, in October 2024 under Russia's chairship.
Statement II is correct: Indonesia joined BRICS as a full member (along with several other nations formally integrated or announced during the expansion phases).
Statement III is incorrect: The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security' (using the term 'Multilateralism' instead of 'Multiculturalism'). This is a classic UPSC single-word substitution trap.
standard_book_ref: Current Affairs - International Relations (The Hindu, Vision IAS Current Affairs)
elimination_trap: Statement III uses 'Multiculturalism' instead of 'Multilateralism', which is a subtle trap designed to test active reading of current affairs themes.

mains_linkage.question: How do regional groupings like BRICS influence the evolving global economic and geopolitical order? Discuss India's role.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I and II are factually correct regarding the summit location, chairship, and Indonesia's membership.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs the two correct statements together.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify the summit location and membership expansion; check thematic terminology carefully.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Statement III is factually incorrect
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement III which contains the incorrect word 'Multiculturalism' instead of 'Multilateralism'.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Uses a distractor containing a subtle keyword substitution in the official theme.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Always check international summit themes word-by-word for diplomatic terminology ('Multilateralism').

option_analysis.label: Trap: Excludes correct statement II
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Indonesia's inclusion as a full member, which was a major update in recent BRICS expansions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Keeps statement I and III, trapping candidates who miss the single-word error in III.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Recognize that Indonesia's full membership status is a correct, verified current affairs fact.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Partial correctness
option_analysis.diagnosis: Misses statement II which is also correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Understates the correct statements by limiting it to only statement I.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Evaluate all statements independently before finalizing the combination.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
question_text:
Consider the following statements about Lokpal :
I. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India.
II. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a Member of the Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory, and only the Chief Justice of India, whether incumbent or retired, has to be its Chairperson.
III. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as the Chairperson or Member, as the case may be.
IV. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: None of the above statements is correct
explanation:
Statement I is incorrect: The Lokpal's jurisdiction extends to public servants of India, including those posted outside India.
Statement II is incorrect: The Chairperson of the Lokpal must be either the Chief Justice of India, a Judge of the Supreme Court, or an eminent person with specified qualifications (it is *not* restricted *only* to the CJI).
Statement III is correct: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, a person shall not be eligible to be appointed as Chairperson or a Member if they are less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office.
Statement IV is incorrect: Lokpal *can* inquire into allegations of corruption against the Prime Minister, subject to certain conditions and exclusions (e.g., relating to international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy, and space).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity (Chapter on Lokpal and Lokayuktas)
elimination_trap: Absolute restrictions like 'only the Chief Justice of India' in statement II and absolute immunity like 'cannot inquire against a sitting Prime Minister' in statement IV are typical UPSC extremes that make statements false.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the institutional challenges faced by the Lokpal in effectively tackling high-level corruption in India.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Only statement III is correct regarding the minimum age requirement (45 years) for the Chairperson or Member of Lokpal.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Requires detailed knowledge of statutory eligibility age under the Lokpal Act, while catching common misconceptions about the Prime Minister and extraterritorial jurisdiction.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Test statutory age limits; eliminate absolute clauses like 'only the CJI' or 'cannot inquire against PM'.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Incorrect inclusion of statement II
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement II is incorrect because the Chairperson position is not restricted *only* to the Chief Justice of India.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs the correct statement III with the flawed statement II.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Remember that Supreme Court judges and eminent persons are also eligible for the post of Lokpal Chairperson.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Incorrect statements I and IV
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I incorrectly restricts jurisdiction within India, and Statement IV incorrectly states Lokpal cannot investigate a sitting PM.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Appeals to cynical views on anti-corruption bodies lacking powers over high offices.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify that Lokpal jurisdiction applies to public servants abroad and includes the Prime Minister with safeguards.

option_analysis.label: Trap: None of the above
option_analysis.diagnosis: Fails to recognize that Statement III is factually correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Triggers doubt since multiple statements are incorrect.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check each statement independently before defaulting to 'None of the above'.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Sports & Current Events
question_text:
Consider the following statements in respect of the first Kho Kho World Cup :
I. The event was held in Delhi, India.
II. Indian men beat Nepal with a score of 78–40 in the final to become the World Champion in men category.
III. Indian women beat Nepal with a score of 54–36 in the final to become the World Champion in women category.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is correct: The inaugural Kho Kho World Cup was hosted in New Delhi, India, in 2025.
Statements II and III contain incorrect match scores or final details regarding the opponent/scores, making them factually inaccurate distractors created around the tournament results.
standard_book_ref: Current Affairs - National Sports Events (The Hindu / PIB)
elimination_trap: Specific numerical sports scores in statements II and III are often fabricated distractors by examiners in sports current affairs.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the potential of indigenous sports in promoting health, culture, and India's soft power globally.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Only statement I is correct as the first Kho Kho World Cup took place in Delhi, India.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests awareness of major indigenous sports tournaments hosted in India.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Be wary of precise numerical scores in sports statements unless double-checked.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Incorrect statements II and III
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements II and III contain incorrect tournament specifics and scores.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes candidates will assume India won every final with specific fabricated statistics.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Reject detailed scorelines unless verified from authentic sports archives.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Incorrect inclusion of statement III
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement III which is factually incorrect.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Mixes the correct venue fact with an incorrect final score detail.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Isolate venue facts from match statistic statements.

option_analysis.label: Trap: All statements correct
option_analysis.diagnosis: Fails to identify that statements II and III contain incorrect score data.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Catches candidates who assume all celebratory news statements about Indian victories are true.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Sports & Achievements
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
I. In the finals of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the world's youngest winner after defeating the Russian player Ian Nepomniachtchi.
II. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world's youngest ever Grandmaster.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is incorrect: The 45th Chess Olympiad held in Budapest, Hungary in 2024 was a *team* event (India won historic gold medals in both open and women's sections), not an individual head-to-head match final against Ian Nepomniachtchi. Gukesh did play brilliantly on board 1, but the framing of a 'final' defeating Nepomniachtchi is factually flawed.
Statement II is correct: Abhimanyu Mishra holds the world record as the youngest person ever to qualify for the title of Chess Grandmaster (achieving the norm at 12 years, 4 months, and 25 days in 2021).
standard_book_ref: Current Affairs - Sports Personalities and Achievements
elimination_trap: Statement I confuses team chess tournaments (like the Chess Olympiad) with World Championship match formats (like the Candidates Tournament or World Championship match).

mains_linkage.question: How has India emerged as a global superpower in chess, nurturing young prodigies? Analyze the factors behind this success.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Incorrect statement I
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I mischaracterizes the Chess Olympiad as a final match against Ian Nepomniachtchi.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Leverages the fame of Gukesh and the 45th Chess Olympiad to insert a false match narrative.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Distinguish between team events (Chess Olympiad) and individual World Championship cycles.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement II is correct; Abhimanyu Mishra holds the record for the youngest ever Grandmaster in chess history.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests accurate knowledge of historic chess records alongside current tournament names.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify youngest Grandmaster records independently of ongoing Olympiad news.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Both statements correct
option_analysis.diagnosis: Assumes statement I is correct because Gukesh and the Chess Olympiad 2024 were major news items.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plays on headline association bias.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check the exact format of the 45th Chess Olympiad before validating statement I.

option_analysis.label: Trap: Neither is correct
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrectly rejects statement II, which is an established factual record in chess.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pushes candidates to doubt all sports statements.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Recognize well-documented records like Abhimanyu Mishra's youngest GM title.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Materials Science / Rare Earth Elements
question_text:
61. Consider the following statements :
Statement I :
Some rare earth elements are used in the manufacture of flat television screens and computer monitors.
Statement II :
Some rare earth elements have phosphorescent properties.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
explanation: Statement I is correct: Rare earth elements (REEs) like europium, terbium, and yttrium are indispensable in the manufacture of flat-screen displays, computer monitors, and LED screens. Statement II is correct and directly explains Statement I: Certain rare earth ions exhibit unique luminescent/phosphorescent properties due to electronic transitions within their 4f electron shells, emitting sharp, pure red (Europium), green (Terbium), and blue colors when stimulated. This phosphorescent capability is the exact scientific reason they are utilized in display screens and monitors. Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Chemistry (The d- and f-Block Elements) / Science Reporter (Rare Earth Applications)
elimination_trap: Understanding that phosphorescence (ability to emit light upon excitation) is the direct physical property utilized in display monitors.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the strategic and industrial significance of rare earth elements in high-technology manufacturing and clean energy, and assess India's supply security.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both statements are correct, and Statement II (phosphorescent properties) directly explains Statement I (usage in display screens).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Evaluates the connection between electronic properties of f-block elements and consumer electronics applications.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Phosphorescent property -> used as phosphors in TV/computer screens.

option_analysis.label: Denies the causal link
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because phosphorescence is the exact reason rare earths produce screen colors.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who fail to connect phosphorescence to screen display technology.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Phosphors on screens emit light via phosphorescence.

option_analysis.label: Doubts rare earth luminescence
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because rare earths are famous for phosphorescent emission.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Questions a well-established property of lanthanides.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Europium and Terbium are classic phosphors.

option_analysis.label: Denies screen manufacturing use
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because rare earths are universally used in flat screens.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Reverses facts.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement I is standard high-tech material knowledge.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Infrastructure & Indigenous Technology (Kavach / Indian Railways)
question_text:
62. Consider the following statements :
I. Indian Railways have prepared a National Rail Plan (NRP) to create a 'future ready' railway system by 2028.
II. 'Kavach' is an Automatic Train Protection system developed in collaboration with Germany.
III. 'Kavach' system consists of RFID tags fitted on track in station section.

Which of the statements given above are not correct?
explanation:
Please note the negative phrasing: 'Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?'
- Statement I is incorrect: The National Rail Plan (NRP) for India was prepared to create a 'future ready' railway system by 2030 (not 2028).
- Statement II is incorrect: 'Kavach' is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system designed and developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in collaboration with three Indian OEMs (Medha, HBL, and Kernex), NOT in collaboration with Germany.
- Statement III is correct: The Kavach architecture involves high-frequency RFID tags installed on railway tracks (trackside) and inside station yards to identify locomotives, train direction, and track occupancy.
Because Statements I and II are incorrect, the correct option answering 'not correct' is (a) I and II only.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Railways Press Releases / PIB Releases on Kavach Deployment and National Rail Plan 2030
elimination_trap: Watch out for the question stem: 'Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?' Many aspirants mark the correct statement by mistake. Also, Kavach is an indigenous Indian innovation, not an imported German collaboration.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the role of indigenous technology in modernizing railway safety in India with special reference to the Kavach Automatic Train Protection system.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I (target year is 2030, not 2028) and II (developed indigenously in India, not with Germany) are both NOT correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Combines a negative stem ('not correct') with testing indigenous technological sovereignty (Kavach).
option_analysis.mental_filter: NRP target is 2030 (I is false); Kavach is indigenous, not German (II is false). Both are NOT correct -> Choose A.

option_analysis.label: Considers Statement III incorrect
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement III is factually correct (RFID tags are integral to Kavach track architecture).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates unsure of the specific physical components of Kavach.
option_analysis.mental_filter: RFID tags on tracks are a defining feature of Kavach.

option_analysis.label: Treats Kavach as German technology
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement II is false and Statement III is true.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Confuses the true/false status of Kavach's origin.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement II is definitely incorrect.

option_analysis.label: Treats all three statements as incorrect
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement III is a true statement, so it cannot be included in 'not correct'.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-inclusive trap for candidates who overlook Statement III's accuracy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement III is correct.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Space Technology & Missions (ISRO)
question_text:
63. Consider the following space missions :
I. Axiom-4
II. SpaDeX
III. Gaganyaan

How many of the space missions given above encourage and support micro-gravity research?
explanation:
Evaluating the three missions:
I. Axiom-4: An international commercial human spaceflight mission to the International Space Station (ISS) in which an ISRO astronaut (Gaganyatri) participates to conduct specific scientific microgravity experiments in biology and material science (Supports microgravity research).
II. SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment): An ISRO twin-satellite mission designed to demonstrate autonomous rendezvous and docking technology in low Earth orbit. Its primary objective is orbital mechanics, autonomous navigation, and docking hardware validation for future space stations and sample return missions, not microgravity research.
III. Gaganyaan: India's human spaceflight mission carrying astronauts and specialized scientific payloads into a 400 km low Earth orbit to conduct microgravity experiments in human physiology, biotechnology, and materials processing (Supports microgravity research).
Therefore, exactly two of the missions (Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan) encourage and support microgravity research.
standard_book_ref: ISRO Mission Profiles / Department of Space Annual Report / Current Affairs on Axiom-4 & Gaganyaan
elimination_trap: Assuming every space mission conducts microgravity research. SpaDeX is strictly a technological demonstration mission for satellite docking.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the scientific and technological significance of India's human spaceflight program (Gaganyaan) and international collaborations in microgravity science.

option_analysis.label: Underestimates microgravity scope
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because both Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan carry microgravity research agendas.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who may think only Gaganyaan does microgravity experiments.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Axiom-4's primary mission aboard ISS is scientific microgravity experimentation.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Only two missions (Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan) support microgravity research, whereas SpaDeX is a satellite docking demonstration.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Fine-grained distinction between experimental science missions and robotic docking engineering demonstrators.
option_analysis.mental_filter: SpaDeX = Space Docking Experiment (docking demo, not microgravity research). Axiom-4 + Gaganyaan = 2.

option_analysis.label: Assumes all space missions do microgravity research
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because SpaDeX is dedicated to demonstrating autonomous docking mechanisms.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-inclusive trap for candidates assuming all space missions conduct microgravity research.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Docking tests like SpaDeX are pure aerospace engineering tests.

option_analysis.label: Denies microgravity research
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because human spaceflight missions are fundamentally microgravity laboratories.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Extreme rejection distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Gaganyaan and Axiom explicitly feature microgravity labs.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Defence Technology / Military Aviation
question_text:
64. With reference to India's defence, consider the following pairs :
Aircraft type | Description
I. Dornier-228 : Maritime patrol aircraft
II. IL-76 : Supersonic combat aircraft
III. C-17 Globemaster III : Military transport aircraft

How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation:
Pair I is correctly matched: The Dornier-228 (manufactured under license by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited) is a twin-turboprop aircraft widely deployed by the Indian Navy and Coast Guard for maritime patrol, coastal surveillance, and search and rescue.
Pair II is incorrectly matched: The Ilyushin Il-76 ('Gajraj') is a four-engine strategic military transport aircraft, NOT a supersonic combat aircraft (fighter jets like Su-30MKI, Rafale, or MiG-29 are supersonic combat aircraft).
Pair III is correctly matched: The Boeing C-17 Globemaster III is a premier strategic heavy-lift military transport aircraft operated by the Indian Air Force for rapid troop and heavy equipment mobility.
Therefore, exactly two pairs (I and III) are correctly matched.
standard_book_ref: Indian Air Force & Indian Navy Official Inventory / Ministry of Defence Annual Report
elimination_trap: Labeling the heavy-lift transport aircraft Il-76 as a 'supersonic combat aircraft' is an unmistakable mismatch.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze India's strategic airlift capabilities and their significance in humanitarian assistance, disaster relief (HADR), and border logistics.

option_analysis.label: Underestimates correctly matched pairs
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because both Dornier-228 and C-17 Globemaster III are correctly matched.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who may not know Dornier's maritime patrol role.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Dornier is Navy/Coast Guard maritime patrol; C-17 is heavy transport.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Exactly two pairs (Dornier-228 and C-17 Globemaster III) are correctly matched; Il-76 is a transport aircraft, not a combat jet.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Basic military aviation classification testing combat vs transport platforms.
option_analysis.mental_filter: IL-76 is a transport plane ('Gajraj'), not a supersonic fighter. 2 pairs correct.

option_analysis.label: Accepts Il-76 as a supersonic fighter
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Il-76 is a subsonic heavy transport aircraft.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests if candidate catches the glaring classification error for Il-76.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Il-76 is a transport giant, not a fighter.

option_analysis.label: Assumes none are correctly matched
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Dornier-228 and C-17 Globemaster III are standard matched pairs.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Extreme rejection option.
option_analysis.mental_filter: C-17 Globemaster III is globally recognized as a military transport aircraft.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Applied Chemistry / Cloud Seeding & Pollution Control
question_text:
65. Artificial way of causing rainfall to reduce air pollution makes use of
(a) silver iodide and potassium iodide
(b) silver nitrate and potassium iodide
(c) silver iodide and potassium nitrate
(d) silver nitrate and potassium chloride
explanation: Cloud seeding (the artificial method of inducing rainfall) disperses cloud condensation nuclei or ice nuclei into suitable clouds to stimulate precipitation, which washes down suspended particulate matter and curbs air pollution. The most effective and standard chemical agents employed are silver iodide (AgI) and potassium iodide (KI) (along with dry ice and sodium chloride). Silver iodide has a hexagonal crystalline structure closely resembling that of ice crystals, making it exceptionally effective as an ice-nucleating agent. Therefore, (a) is the correct answer.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Chemistry (Surface Chemistry / Colloids) / Down To Earth (IIT Kanpur Cloud Seeding Experiments)
elimination_trap: Confusing silver iodide (AgI) with silver nitrate (AgNO3). Silver nitrate is a laboratory staining agent and toxic salt, not used for cloud seeding.

mains_linkage.question: Critically evaluate the efficacy and environmental impacts of artificial rain (cloud seeding) as a short-term intervention against winter smog in urban India.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Silver iodide (AgI) and potassium iodide (KI) are the standard chemicals used in meteorological cloud seeding operations.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Direct chemical identification spurred by high-profile trial projects in Delhi by IIT Kanpur.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Cloud seeding = Silver Iodide (AgI) + Potassium Iodide (KI).

option_analysis.label: Substitutes silver nitrate for silver iodide
option_analysis.diagnosis: Silver nitrate (AgNO3) does not have the ice-mimicking crystal lattice required for ice nucleation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Classic chemistry naming confusion (iodide vs nitrate).
option_analysis.mental_filter: Iodide, not nitrate, mimics ice crystals.

option_analysis.label: Substitutes potassium nitrate for potassium iodide
option_analysis.diagnosis: Potassium nitrate is an oxidizer/fertilizer, not an atmospheric seeding nucleus.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Mixes silver iodide with an unviable nitrate salt.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Look for iodides: silver iodide and potassium iodide.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect salts entirely
option_analysis.diagnosis: Neither silver nitrate nor potassium chloride is the standard seeding formulation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plausible inorganic salts distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Silver iodide is the quintessential cloud seeding chemical.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Presidential Powers / Article 72 Pardoning Power
question_text:
66. Consider the following statements with regard to pardoning power of the President of India :
I. The exercise of this power by the President can be subjected to limited judicial review.
II. The President can exercise this power without the advice of the Central Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is correct: In landmark judgments including Maru Ram v. Union of India (1980), Kehar Singh v. Union of India (1989), and Epuru Sudhakar v. Govt. of A.P. (2006), the Supreme Court ruled that while the merits of the President's decision under Article 72 cannot be sat in appeal upon by courts, the exercise of pardoning power is subject to limited judicial review on established grounds such as arbitrariness, mala fide, extraneous considerations, or non-application of mind.
Statement II is incorrect: Under the constitutional framework of parliamentary democracy and Article 74(1), the President does NOT act independently in exercising the pardoning power; he/she must act strictly on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers (communicated through the Ministry of Home Affairs).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth Indian Polity (Chapter: President) / Constitution of India (Article 72 and Article 74)
elimination_trap: Thinking that executive clemency is a discretionary personal prerogative of the President. In India, the President is bound by the advice of the Union Cabinet.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the scope and limits of judicial review over the pardoning power of the President under Article 72 of the Constitution.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is correct (limited judicial review on grounds of mala fide/arbitrariness), while Statement II is incorrect as the President is bound by the aid and advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the intersection of Article 72 (pardoning power) with Article 74 (mandatory Cabinet advice) and Supreme Court jurisprudence.
option_analysis.mental_filter: President's pardon is bound by Cabinet advice (II is false) and subject to limited judicial review (I is true).

option_analysis.label: Treats pardon as personal presidential discretion
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the President has no discretionary power under Article 72.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who confuse monarchical prerogative with constitutional presidency.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The President cannot act without Central Government advice.

option_analysis.label: Accepts independent presidential discretion
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement II violates Article 74(1).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Common distractor combining judicial review with absolute executive autonomy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Article 74 binds the President to Cabinet advice.

option_analysis.label: Denies judicial review over executive clemency
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the Supreme Court has repeatedly upheld limited judicial review.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Relies on obsolete view that pardons are non-justiciable.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Epuru Sudhakar and Maru Ram established limited judicial review.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Parliament / Office of the Speaker
question_text:
67. Consider the following statements :
I. On the dissolution of the House of the People, the Speaker shall not vacate his/her office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
II. According to the provisions of the Constitution of India, a Member of the House of the People on being elected as Speaker shall resign from his/her political party immediately.
III. The Speaker of the House of the People may be removed from his/her office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then Members of the House, provided that no resolution shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move the resolution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is correct: Under the second proviso to Article 94 of the Constitution, whenever the House of the People is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution.
Statement II is incorrect: There is no provision in the Constitution of India requiring the Speaker to resign from his/her political party upon election (unlike the British convention 'once a speaker, always a speaker'). While Paragraph 5 of the Tenth Schedule provides that if a Speaker voluntarily resigns from his party, he will not be disqualified under the anti-defection law, it is not mandatory to resign.
Statement III is correct: Under Article 94(c), the Speaker may be removed from office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by an effective majority ('a majority of all the then members of the House'), provided that no resolution for this purpose shall be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given.
Therefore, Statements I and III are correct.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth Indian Polity (Chapter: Parliament) / Constitution of India (Article 94)
elimination_trap: Confusing British parliamentary convention with Indian constitutional law. In the UK, the Speaker resigns from their political party; in India, there is no constitutional mandate to resign.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the constitutional role and neutrality of the Office of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha in light of parliamentary conventions and judicial pronouncements.

option_analysis.label: Believes Speaker must constitutionally resign from party
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the Indian Constitution does not mandate the Speaker to resign from their political party.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits British parliamentary convention vs Indian constitutional reality.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Indian Speakers remain party members; Tenth Schedule allows them to resign without defection penalty, but does not mandate it.

option_analysis.label: Omits Speaker's continuity after dissolution
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is a literal reproduction of Article 94 proviso.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who think dissolution ends the Speaker's tenure immediately.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Speaker continues in office until the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I and III are verbatim constitutional provisions under Article 94, while Statement II is false.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard Indian Polity question testing exact provisions of Article 94 and political party conventions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Speaker stays till first meeting of new Lok Sabha (I); does not need to resign from party (II is false); removed by effective majority with 14 days' notice (III).

option_analysis.label: Accepts all statements
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement II is false.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-inclusive trap.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Eliminate Statement II.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Parliament / Tenth Schedule & Anti-Defection Law
question_text:
68. Consider the following statements :
I. If any question arises as to whether a Member of the House of the People has become subject to disqualification under the 10th Schedule, the President's decision in accordance with the opinion of the Council of Union Ministers shall be final.
II. There is no mention of the word 'political party' in the Constitution of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Statement I is incorrect: Under Paragraph 6(1) of the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India, questions regarding disqualification on ground of defection are decided by the Chairman or the Speaker of the respective House (not the President). Disqualification on constitutional grounds under Article 102(1) is decided by the President under Article 103, but in accordance with the opinion of the Election Commission of India, NOT the Council of Union Ministers.
Statement II is incorrect: The term 'political party' is explicitly mentioned multiple times in the Constitution of India, most prominently throughout the Tenth Schedule (inserted by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985) and in Article 75(1B) and Article 164(1B) (inserted by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003).
Therefore, neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth Indian Polity (Chapter: Anti-Defection Law / Tenth Schedule) / Constitution of India
elimination_trap: Confusing who decides disqualification under Article 103 (President acting on ECI opinion) vs Tenth Schedule (Presiding Officer of the House). Also, believing the popular myth that 'political party' is never mentioned in the Constitution (it was formally added in 1985 via the Tenth Schedule).

mains_linkage.question: Critically evaluate the efficacy of the Tenth Schedule in curbing political defections in India. Does vesting adjudicatory authority in the Presiding Officer compromise neutrality?

option_analysis.label: Confuses deciding authority under Tenth Schedule
option_analysis.diagnosis: Disqualification under Tenth Schedule is decided exclusively by the Speaker/Chairman, not the President.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Combines Tenth Schedule with Article 103 and misattributes advice to the Council of Ministers.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Tenth Schedule = Speaker/Chairman decides. President has no role.

option_analysis.label: Believes 'political party' is absent from Constitution
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the 52nd Amendment (1985) formally inserted 'political party' into the Tenth Schedule.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits the historical fact that the original 1950 Constitution did not mention political parties, ignoring constitutional amendments.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The Tenth Schedule and 91st Amendment explicitly mention 'political party'.

option_analysis.label: Accepts both false propositions
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because both statements are factually wrong.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Double distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Both statements are false.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Neither Statement I nor Statement II is correct.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests exact constitutional text regarding anti-defection and constitutional amendment history.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement I is false (Speaker decides, not President); Statement II is false (Tenth Schedule explicitly mentions political parties).

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Mineral Laws & Centre-State Relations
question_text:
69. Consider the following statements :
Statement I :
In India, State Governments have no power for making rules for grant of concessions in respect of extraction of minor minerals even though such minerals are located in their territories.
Statement II :
In India, the Central Government has the power to notify minor minerals under the relevant law.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
explanation:
Under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) (MMDR) Act, 1957:
- Statement I is incorrect: Section 15 of the MMDR Act, 1957 explicitly empowers State Governments to make rules for regulating the grant of quarry leases, mining leases, or other mineral concessions in respect of minor minerals and for purposes connected therewith. State Governments have plenary rule-making authority over minor minerals located in their territories.
- Statement II is correct: Section 3(e) of the MMDR Act, 1957 defines minor minerals (such as building stones, gravel, ordinary clay, ordinary sand) and explicitly empowers the Central Government to notify any other mineral as a 'minor mineral' by notification in the Official Gazette (as was done for 31 non-metallic minerals in 2015).
Hence, Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct.
standard_book_ref: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (Sections 3(e) and 15) / Ministry of Mines Annual Report
elimination_trap: A recurring UPSC theme: State Governments hold exclusive administrative and regulatory power to grant concessions and frame rules for 'minor minerals', while the Central Government has the statutory power to classify/notify which minerals are 'minor minerals'.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the division of regulatory powers between the Union and the States regarding major and minor minerals under the MMDR Act, 1957.

option_analysis.label: Assumes States have no power over minor minerals
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Section 15 of MMDR Act gives States the exclusive power to make rules for minor mineral concessions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits confusion between central notification power and state concession-granting power.
option_analysis.mental_filter: States have full power to make rules for minor minerals.

option_analysis.label: Treats both statements as true
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement I denies state regulatory power.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who assume the Centre controls all mineral licensing.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement I is legally false.

option_analysis.label: Inverts the truth of the statements
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the Central Government definitely has statutory power to notify minor minerals.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Reverses statutory powers.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Central Government notifies minor minerals under Sec 3(e).

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is not correct (States possess full rule-making power for minor minerals under Section 15), but Statement II is correct (Centre notifies minor minerals under Section 3(e)).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Classic UPSC question format examining federal division of mineral rights under the MMDR Act.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Centre notifies minor minerals (II is true); States regulate concessions and royalty for them (I is false).

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Global Environmental Governance & Legislation
question_text:
70. Which organization has enacted the Nature Restoration Law (NRL) to tackle climate change and biodiversity loss?
(a) The European Union
(b) The World Bank
(c) The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
(d) The Food and Agriculture Organization
options: The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development
explanation: The Nature Restoration Law (NRL) was enacted by the European Union (EU) in 2024 as a cornerstone of the European Green Deal and the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030. It is a pioneering, legally binding regulation that mandates EU member states to put restoration measures in place covering at least 20% of the EU's land and sea areas by 2030, and all ecosystems in need of restoration by 2050, aiming to reverse biodiversity decline and enhance carbon sequestration.
standard_book_ref: European Commission Environment / Down To Earth / The Hindu International Environmental Policy
elimination_trap: NRL is a landmark piece of binding regional legislation enacted by the European Union, whereas entities like the World Bank or OECD are financial/economic advisory bodies that do not 'enact laws'.

mains_linkage.question: Assess the significance of legally binding ecological restoration targets such as the EU Nature Restoration Law in fulfilling the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: The European Union enacted the Nature Restoration Law (NRL) as part of the European Green Deal.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Direct institutional knowledge check on landmark global environmental legislation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Nature Restoration Law (NRL) = European Union (EU).

option_analysis.label: Multilateral financial institution distractor
option_analysis.diagnosis: The World Bank is a multilateral development lender and does not enact legislation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Uses a prominent international institution.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Banks provide loans; they do not enact restoration laws.

option_analysis.label: Economic policy forum distractor
option_analysis.diagnosis: The OECD is a intergovernmental policy organization without legislative enactment powers.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plausible multilateral organization option.
option_analysis.mental_filter: OECD does not pass binding laws.

option_analysis.label: UN specialized agency distractor
option_analysis.diagnosis: The FAO sets international food standards and agricultural guidance, but did not enact this law.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates based on the natural resources mandate of FAO.
option_analysis.mental_filter: NRL is European Union law.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Fiscal Policy & Deficit Metrics
question_text:
71. Suppose the revenue expenditure is ₹ 80,000 crores and the revenue receipts of the Government are ₹ 60,000 crores. The Government budget also shows borrowings of ₹ 10,000 crores and interest payments of ₹ 6,000 crores. Which of the following statements are correct?
I. Revenue deficit is ₹ 20,000 crores.
II. Fiscal deficit is ₹ 10,000 crores.
III. Primary deficit is ₹ 4,000 crores.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
Let us calculate each deficit metric using standard NCERT macroeconomics formulas:
1. Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts
   = ₹ 80,000 crores - ₹ 60,000 crores = ₹ 20,000 crores. (Statement I is correct)
2. Fiscal Deficit = Total Borrowings of the Government
   By definition, Fiscal Deficit equals the total borrowing requirement of the government, given here as ₹ 10,000 crores. (Statement II is correct)
3. Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments
   = ₹ 10,000 crores - ₹ 6,000 crores = ₹ 4,000 crores. (Statement III is correct)
Therefore, all three statements (I, II, and III) are correct.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics (Chapter 5: Government Budget and the Economy) / Ramesh Singh Indian Economy
elimination_trap: Remembering that Fiscal Deficit is fundamentally identical to the Government's total net borrowings.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the macroeconomic significance of Revenue Deficit, Fiscal Deficit, and Primary Deficit. Why is targeting the primary deficit crucial for debt sustainability?

option_analysis.label: Omits primary deficit calculation
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement III is mathematically verified (10,000 - 6,000 = 4,000).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Excludes the final deficit metric.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments.

option_analysis.label: Omits revenue deficit calculation
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is a straightforward subtraction (80,000 - 60,000 = 20,000).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Excludes the most basic deficit calculation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts.

option_analysis.label: Omits fiscal deficit calculation
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement II is correct because Fiscal Deficit = Borrowings.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates who fail to equate Fiscal Deficit with Borrowings.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Fiscal Deficit is defined as total borrowing.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: All three statements are mathematically and conceptually correct based on standard macroeconomic definitions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Direct numerical calculation testing mastery of core deficit formulas.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Rev Deficit = 20k, Fiscal Deficit = 10k, Primary Deficit = 4k -> All I, II, and III are correct.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Transport Corridors & Geopolitics
question_text:
72. India is one of the founding members of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), a multimodal transportation corridor, which will connect
(a) India to Central Asia to Europe via Iran
(b) India to Central Asia via China
(c) India to South-East Asia through Bangladesh and Myanmar
(d) India to Europe through Azerbaijan
options: India to Central Asia to Europe via Iran
India to Central Asia via China
India to South-East Asia through Bangladesh and Myanmar
explanation: The International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) is a 7,200-km multi-mode transport network of ship, rail, and road routes established in September 2000 by its founding members: India, Iran, and Russia. Its primary route connects India (from ports like Mumbai/JNPT) across the Arabian Sea to Iran's ports (Bandar Abbas / Chabahar), moving overland through Iran to the Caspian Sea / Central Asia and onward to Russia and Northern/Western Europe, dramatically cutting freight transit time and cost compared to the Suez Canal route. Therefore, (a) accurately describes the corridor.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII India: People and Economy (Transport and Communication) / Ministry of External Affairs Factsheet on INSTC
elimination_trap: Option (d) mentions Azerbaijan, but INSTC's defining transit gateway from India is via Iran across the sea. Option (b) mentions China (incorrect) and (c) describes the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, not INSTC.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the geostrategic and economic significance of the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) for India's connectivity with Central Asia and Eurasia.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: INSTC connects India to Central Asia and Europe via Iran through a multimodal network.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Clear identification of the primary strategic transit corridor linking India with Eurasia.
option_analysis.mental_filter: INSTC = India -> Sea to Iran (Bandar Abbas/Chabahar) -> Caspian Sea/Central Asia -> Russia/Europe.

option_analysis.label: Incorporates China into route
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because INSTC bypasses China completely.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Geographical mismatch.
option_analysis.mental_filter: INSTC does not transit through China.

option_analysis.label: Confuses with Southeast Asian Trilateral Highway
option_analysis.diagnosis: Connecting to Southeast Asia via Myanmar is the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway / Kaladan project.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Swaps the North-South corridor with East-West connectivity initiatives.
option_analysis.mental_filter: North-South Corridor goes to Russia/Europe, not Southeast Asia.

option_analysis.label: Omits Iran as the initial transit hub
option_analysis.diagnosis: India has no direct maritime or land link to Azerbaijan without transiting through Iran.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Names an intermediate corridor member while omitting the primary entry gateway.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Iran is the indispensable gateway connecting India to the rest of the corridor.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Economic Geography / Biofuels & Energy Resources
question_text:
73. Consider the following statements :
Statement I :
Of the two major ethanol producers in the world, i.e., Brazil and the United States of America, the former produces more ethanol than the latter.
Statement II :
Unlike in the United States of America where corn is the principal feedstock for ethanol production, sugarcane is the principal feedstock for ethanol production in Brazil.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
explanation:
Statement I is incorrect: The United States of America is the world's largest producer of ethanol, accounting for over 53% of global output, while Brazil is the second-largest producer, accounting for about 28% of global production. The statement claims that Brazil ('the former') produces more ethanol than the USA ('the latter'), which is factually false.
Statement II is correct: In the United States, corn (maize) serves as the primary feedstock (accounting for >90% of US ethanol production), whereas in Brazil, sugarcane juice and molasses are the predominant feedstock for ethanol production.
Therefore, Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct.
standard_book_ref: Renewable Fuels Association (RFA) Global Ethanol Statistics / NCERT Class XII Fundamentals of Human Geography
elimination_trap: Watch the terms 'the former' and 'the latter'. Brazil is listed first, but the US is the undisputed #1 producer of ethanol in the world.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze the global feedstock dynamics in biofuel production and examine the prospects and challenges of India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP).

option_analysis.label: Believes Brazil produces more ethanol than USA
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because the United States produces significantly more ethanol than Brazil.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits Brazil's historical fame as an early pioneer in sugarcane flex-fuel cars.
option_analysis.mental_filter: USA produces >50% of global ethanol; Brazil is #2. Statement I is false.

option_analysis.label: Treats Statement I as true
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement I contains an inverted ranking.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tempts candidates based on feedstock knowledge while missing the production hierarchy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statement I is false.

option_analysis.label: Reverses truth of the two statements
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because Statement II correctly identifies corn in the US and sugarcane in Brazil.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubts the well-known feedstock distribution.
option_analysis.mental_filter: US = Corn ethanol; Brazil = Sugarcane ethanol.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is not correct (USA produces more than Brazil), but Statement II is correct (US uses corn; Brazil uses sugarcane).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Precision check on global agricultural energy commodities and feedstock differentiation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Global ethanol: USA > Brazil (I is false); USA uses corn, Brazil uses sugarcane (II is true).

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Climate Change / Wet-Bulb Temperature & Heat Stress
question_text:
74. The World Bank warned that India could become one of the first places where wet-bulb temperatures routinely exceed 35 °C. Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the above-said report?
I. Peninsular India will most likely suffer from flooding, tropical cyclones and droughts.
II. The survival of animals including humans will be affected as shedding of their body heat through perspiration becomes difficult.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
explanation:
The World Bank report titled 'Climate Investment Opportunities in India's Cooling Sector' highlighted alarming climate vulnerability projections for India:
- Statement I is reflected: The report details how compounding climate extremes—such as erratic monsoon shifts leading to severe floods, intensified tropical cyclones along the peninsular coastline, and severe recurring droughts—will impact peninsular and coastal India.
- Statement II is reflected: A wet-bulb temperature of 35 °C represents the absolute physiological upper limit of human survivability. At this threshold (combining 35 °C with 100% relative humidity), the human body is unable to shed metabolic heat through the evaporation of perspiration (sweating), causing internal core body temperature to rise rapidly to fatal levels of heatstroke and organ failure in humans and animals.
Both statements accurately capture the severe implications highlighted by the report.
standard_book_ref: World Bank Report: 'Climate Investment Opportunities in India's Cooling Sector' (2022) / Down To Earth
elimination_trap: Some candidates think wet-bulb temperature only relates to physiological heat stress (Statement II) and disregard Statement I, but the World Bank report explicitly framed wet-bulb extremes within India's broader vulnerability to hydrometeorological disasters (floods, cyclones, droughts).

mains_linkage.question: Explain the concept of 'wet-bulb temperature'. Discuss its socio-economic and public health implications for India's labor-intensive sectors.

option_analysis.label: Omits the physiological impact of wet-bulb temperature
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement II is the quintessential scientific definition of wet-bulb survivability threshold.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Excludes the primary physiological definition of wet-bulb heat.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Wet-bulb >35°C prevents perspiration cooling.

option_analysis.label: Omits broader hydrometeorological impacts in report
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement I is an integral part of the climate vulnerability findings in the World Bank report.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Restricts the question only to biophysical definitions while ignoring the report's macro-disaster context.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The World Bank report covers both extreme weather events and physiological heat thresholds.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both Statement I (vulnerability to floods, cyclones, and droughts) and Statement II (physiological failure of heat dissipation via sweating at 35°C wet-bulb) reflect the report.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Integrates physical climatology with biometeorological limits of mammalian survival.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Wet-bulb heatwave extremes occur alongside compound climate disasters (Both I and II).

option_analysis.label: Rejects report findings
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because both statements accurately describe the report's findings.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Extreme rejection option.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Both statements reflect real climate risks highlighted by the World Bank.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Government Budgeting & Deficit Calculation
question_text:
75. A country's fiscal deficit stands at ₹ 50,000 crores. It is receiving ₹ 10,000 crores through non-debt creating capital receipts. The country's interest liabilities are ₹ 1,500 crores. What is the gross primary deficit?
(a) ₹ 48,500 crores
(b) ₹ 51,500 crores
(c) ₹ 58,500 crores
(d) None of the above
explanation:
By standard macroeconomic definition in public finance:
Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit - Net Interest Liabilities
Given data:
- Gross Fiscal Deficit = ₹ 50,000 crores
- Interest Liabilities = ₹ 1,500 crores
- Non-debt creating capital receipts = ₹ 10,000 crores (this figure is extraneous distractor information, as it is already accounted for in arriving at the Fiscal Deficit figure).
Calculating Gross Primary Deficit:
Gross Primary Deficit = ₹ 50,000 crores - ₹ 1,500 crores = ₹ 48,500 crores.
Therefore, (a) is the correct answer.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII Macroeconomics (Chapter 5: Government Budget and the Economy) / Ramesh Singh Indian Economy
elimination_trap: The inclusion of 'non-debt creating capital receipts of ₹ 10,000 crores' is an examiner trap meant to induce arithmetic confusion. Non-debt capital receipts are already subtracted while computing the Fiscal Deficit.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the importance of the primary deficit metric in evaluating current fiscal stance versus accumulated legacy debt obligations.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Gross Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit (₹ 50,000 cr) - Interest Liabilities (₹ 1,500 cr) = ₹ 48,500 crores.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the exact formula for primary deficit while filtering out redundant budget figures.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Liabilities = 50,000 - 1,500 = 48,500.

option_analysis.label: Adds interest liability instead of subtracting
option_analysis.diagnosis: Erroneously calculates Fiscal Deficit + Interest Liabilities (50,000 + 1,500 = 51,500).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Mathematical operator inversion error.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Primary deficit subtracts interest payments, never adds them.

option_analysis.label: Muddles non-debt receipts with interest
option_analysis.diagnosis: Erroneously incorporates the ₹ 10,000 crore distractor.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Traps candidates who attempt to factor in non-debt capital receipts.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Ignore non-debt capital receipts when fiscal deficit is already given.

option_analysis.label: Skeptical 'None of the above' trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrect because ₹ 48,500 crores is present as option (a).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard 'None of the above' distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The exact calculated value is present in option A.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Fiscal Federalism & Finance Commission
question_text:
Which of the following statements with regard to recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission of India are correct?
I. It has recommended grants of ₹4,800 crores from the year 2022-23 to the year 2025-26 for incentivizing States to enhance educational outcomes.
II. 45% of the net proceeds of Union taxes are to be shared with States.
III. ₹45,000 crores are to be kept as performance-based incentive for all States for carrying out agricultural reforms.
IV. It reintroduced tax effort criteria to reward fiscal performance.
explanation: Statement I is correct: The 15th Finance Commission recommended sector-specific grants including educational sector grants and grants for incentivizing States to enhance educational outcomes. Statement II is incorrect: The horizontal/vertical devolution vertical share of divisible pool recommended by the 15th Finance Commission is 41%, not 45% (which was recommended by the 14th Finance Commission). Statement III is correct: The Commission recommended performance-based incentives for agricultural reforms amounting to ₹45,000 crores. Statement IV is correct: It reintroduced the 'tax effort' criterion with a weightage to reward states that have made better tax mobilization efforts relative to their gross state domestic product (GSDP). Thus, statements I, III, and IV are correct.
standard_book_ref: Ramesh Singh (Indian Economy); 15th Finance Commission Report Vol-I
elimination_trap: Statement II is a classic stat-swap trap used by UPSC. Aspirants often confuse the 42%/41% devolution of the 15th FC with the 42% or 45% figures. Recalling that 14th FC gave 42% and 15th FC reduced it to 41% helps eliminate statements containing II.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission and their implications on fiscal federalism in India.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II which states 45% devolution, whereas the actual devolution recommended by the 15th Finance Commission is 41%.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs correct statements with a subtly altered historical data point.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Always double-check vertical devolution percentage: 14th FC was 42%, 15th FC is 41%.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II (45% tax share instead of 41%), making it incorrect.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Mixes correct fiscal reform recommendations with incorrect vertical tax devolution share.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check vertical devolution first to eliminate half the options.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I, III, and IV are factually correct recommendations of the 15th Finance Commission regarding education sector grants, agricultural reform incentives, and tax effort criteria respectively.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Requires detailed knowledge of sector-specific and performance-based grants under the 15th FC report.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Verify tax effort criterion and agriculture incentive allocation figures from the 15th FC summary.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II (45% share), which is factually inaccurate.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Relies on candidate missing the exact percentage change between the 14th and 15th Finance Commissions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Remember that vertical share was brought down from 42% to 41% to account for newly formed UTs of J&K and Ladakh.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: International Financial Institutions
question_text:
Consider the following statements in respect of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) :
I. It provides loans and guarantees to middle income countries.
II. It works single-handedly to help developing countries to reduce poverty.
III. It was established to help Europe rebuild after the World War II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
explanation: Statement I is correct: IBRD provides commercial-grade loans and guarantees to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries. Statement II is incorrect: IBRD does not work 'single-handedly'; it is part of the World Bank Group (which includes IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID) and collaborates with various international organizations to reduce poverty. Statement III is correct: IBRD was originally established in 1944 (as part of the Bretton Woods institutions) primarily to assist in the reconstruction of post-World War II Europe.
standard_book_ref: Ramesh Singh (Indian Economy - International Financial Institutions)
elimination_trap: The word 'single-handedly' in Statement II is an absolute, extreme term that almost always signals a false statement in UPSC questions.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the role of Bretton Woods institutions in global economic governance and poverty alleviation.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II, which claims IBRD works 'single-handedly', ignoring the World Bank Group structure.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Uses extreme restrictive/exclusive language ('single-handedly') to trap candidates.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Watch out for absolute words like 'only', 'exclusively', 'single-handedly'.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits statement I which correctly identifies IBRD's core mandate of lending to middle-income countries.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Separates core functional definitions from historical origins.
option_analysis.mental_filter: IBRD focuses on middle-income countries while IDA focuses on the poorest countries.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements I and III are correct. IBRD targets middle-income/creditworthy low-income nations and was founded post-WWII in 1944 for European reconstruction.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests foundational knowledge of World Bank Group entities and their historical genesis.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Use the extreme-word elimination rule on Statement II to easily arrive at I and III.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II, making it incorrect due to the unrealistic claim of 'single-handed' operation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-inclusive trap option for candidates who fail to spot the extreme wording in statement II.
option_analysis.mental_filter: No single international financial institution works 'single-handedly'.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Banking & Payment Systems
question_text:
Consider the following statements in respect of RTGS and NEFT :
I. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time to settle payments.
II. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.
III. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.
explanation: Statement I is correct: RTGS (Real Time Gross Settlement) settles transactions on a real-time basis (instantaneous), whereas NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer) settles transactions in batches at designated times. Statement II is incorrect: As per RBI guidelines, banks cannot levy any charges on inward transactions for both NEFT and RTGS. Statement III is incorrect: Both RTGS and NEFT operate 24x7x365 days a year; neither has restricted operating hours on certain days.
standard_book_ref: RBI Circulars on NEFT/RTGS 24x7 operations; Ramesh Singh (Indian Economy)
elimination_trap: Aspirants often assume NEFT or RTGS has banking-hour restrictions or charges for inward transactions, missing RBI's zero-charge rule for inward remittances.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the evolution of digital payment systems in India and their impact on financial inclusion.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Only Statement I is correct. RTGS provides real-time settlement, while NEFT settles in batches. Statements II and III are wrong as RBI prohibits inward transaction charges for both, and both operate 24x7.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests deep operational guidelines of RBI payment mechanisms.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Recall RBI's 24x7 availability mandate and zero-charge policy for inward digital transfers.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement II, which incorrectly states that customers are charged for RTGS inward transactions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Capitalizes on common misconceptions regarding bank service fees on large-value transfers.
option_analysis.mental_filter: RBI guidelines explicitly bar banks from charging customers for inward NEFT/RTGS.

option_analysis.label: Incorrect Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes statement III, which incorrectly claims NEFT has different operating hours from RTGS (both are 24x7).
