option_analysis.mental_filter: NSDL deals with securities and demat accounts.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) operates the National Financial Switch (NFS) linking all ATMs.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests knowledge of India's umbrella retail payments operating organization.
option_analysis.mental_filter: All inter-bank retail ATM routing happens via NPCI's National Financial Switch.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: RBI is the apex central bank and regulator; it created NPCI under PSS Act 2007 to operate retail payment infrastructure.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Classic regulator vs operating entity confusion.
option_analysis.mental_filter: RBI regulates; NPCI operates retail payments.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Banking Regulations - Capital Adequacy Ratio & Basel Norms
question_text:
Consider the following statements: 
•  Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if any account-holders fail to repay dues. 
•  CAR is decided by each individual bank. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is correct: Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), also known as Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR), is the ratio of a bank's capital (Tier 1 and Tier 2) to its risk-weighted assets. It represents the cushion of own funds banks must maintain to absorb potential credit losses if borrowers default on loans, protecting depositors.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: CAR is NOT decided by each individual bank. It is mandated and regulated by the central bank (Reserve Bank of India in India) in accordance with international Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) standards (Basel III norms).
standard_book_ref: Ramesh Singh - Indian Economy (Chapter: Banking in India - Capital Adequacy Norms); Basel III Regulatory Framework
elimination_trap: Statement 2 gives autonomy to commercial banks, whereas prudential capital buffers are strictly regulatory mandates set by the central bank.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the importance of the Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) in maintaining financial stability and discuss challenges faced by PSBs in meeting Basel III norms.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is correct (CAR is bank's own capital to absorb asset losses) and Statement 2 is false (decided by RBI, not individual banks).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Accurately distinguishes between banking risk buffer definition and regulatory determination.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Central banks enforce prudential norms to prevent bank insolvency.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is false; if banks decided their own CAR, moral hazard would lead to reckless risk-taking.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests common sense in financial regulation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: No bank can arbitrarily fix its own capital adequacy requirements.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Accepts Statement 2, which contradicts the entire premise of Basel banking supervision.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Traps candidates who misinterpret bank internal risk ratings as setting statutory CAR.
option_analysis.mental_filter: RBI mandates minimum CRAR (e.g. 9% for scheduled commercial banks).

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is the fundamental economic textbook definition of Capital Adequacy Ratio.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Over-skeptical trap on core banking terminology.
option_analysis.mental_filter: CAR = Capital / Risk-Weighted Assets.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Digital Public Infrastructure - India Stack & Aadhaar Architecture
question_text:
The identity platform ‘Aadhaar‘ provides open “Application Programming Interfaces (APIs)”. What does it imply? 
•  It can be integrated into any electronic device. 
•  Online authentication using iris is possible. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is correct: The identity platform 'Aadhaar' provides open Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). This open architecture allows Aadhaar authentication and e-KYC services to be integrated into any electronic device (such as biometric micro-ATMs, smartphones, PoS devices, and tablets).
2. Statement 2 is correct: The Aadhaar authentication framework supports multi-modal biometric authentication, including fingerprint scans, iris scans, and facial recognition, alongside OTP-based online authentication.
standard_book_ref: UIDAI Technical Architecture Documents; India Stack Specifications; Science & Technology Annual Updates
elimination_trap: Aspirants often doubt Statement 1 due to the word 'any electronic device', but an open API by definition enables software integration on any device capable of executing the client code and connecting to UIDAI servers.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the role of open Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) in developing India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and enhancing governance delivery.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Statement 2, even though iris-based biometric authentication is an official, built-in capability of Aadhaar.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubts biometric modalities supported by UIDAI.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Iris scans are officially captured and authenticated by UIDAI.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Doubts Statement 1 because of the word 'any', failing to understand open API interoperability.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits fear of extreme words ('any electronic device').
option_analysis.mental_filter: Open APIs are platform-agnostic and allow universal device integration.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both 1 and 2 are correct. Open APIs permit universal device integration, and iris authentication is operational.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests understanding of the technical modularity of India Stack.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Open APIs imply device-agnostic integration + iris scanning is a core Aadhaar biometric.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Rejects both true technical characteristics of the Aadhaar system.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Cynical trap on technology features.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Both capabilities are fundamental to Aadhaar's architecture.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Geopolitics & Humanitarian Geography - Conflict & Famine Zones
question_text: Very recently, in which of the following countries have lakhs of people either suffered from severe famine/acute malnutrition or died due to starvation caused by war/ethnic conﬂicts?
explanation:
Around 2017-2018, the United Nations declared severe famine and acute food insecurity crises in four countries: Yemen, South Sudan, Somalia, and northeastern Nigeria.
In Yemen, prolonged civil war and naval blockades created the world's worst man-made humanitarian crisis with millions facing starvation.
In South Sudan, ongoing civil conflict, displacement, and economic collapse caused official famine declarations in several counties.
standard_book_ref: UN World Food Programme (WFP) Global Report on Food Crises 2017-2018; Contemporary Global Geopolitics
elimination_trap: Candidates often think of Venezuela due to economic hyperinflation, but acute mass starvation and official famine alerts specifically engulfed Yemen and South Sudan.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the weaponization of food and humanitarian crises in contemporary conflicts, citing global hot spots.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Angola and Zambia were not experiencing mass starvation or famine emergencies in 2017-2018.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Presents stable Southern African nations as distractors.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Famines were driven by active armed warfare, not peaceful Southern Africa.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Morocco and Tunisia are middle-income North African nations without severe famine conditions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: North African distractors.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Morocco and Tunisia have stable food distribution.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Venezuela faced hyperinflation and food shortages, but was not classified under the catastrophic UN famine alerts like Yemen.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits high media coverage of Venezuelan migration and food queues.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Official UN famine declarations were issued for South Sudan and Yemen.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Yemen and South Sudan experienced catastrophic famines and acute malnutrition caused by prolonged civil warfare.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Focuses on prominent international humanitarian disasters of the era.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Yemen and South Sudan were the two primary nations in UN Level-3 famine emergencies.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Modern Indian History - Colonial Education Policy (Wood's Despatch)
question_text:
Regarding Wood’s Dispatch, which of the following statements are true? 
•  Grants-in-Aid system was introduced. 
•  Establishment of universities was recommended. 
•  English as a medium of instruction at all levels of education was recommended. 
 Select the correct answer using the code given below:
explanation:
Wood's Despatch of 1854 (considered the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'):
1. Statement 1 is correct: It recommended the introduction of a comprehensive grants-in-aid system to encourage private enterprise and voluntary efforts in education.
2. Statement 2 is correct: It recommended the establishment of universities on the model of London University in the presidency towns of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras (which were established in 1857).
3. Statement 3 is incorrect: It did NOT recommend English as the medium of instruction at all levels. Instead, it explicitly prescribed vernacular languages for primary school education, Anglo-vernacular in high schools, and English for higher/university education.
standard_book_ref: Spectrum - A Brief History of Modern India (Chapter: Development of Education under British Rule); Bipan Chandra - Modern India
elimination_trap: The word 'all levels' in Statement 3 is a definitive extreme trap. Wood's Despatch championed vernacular education at the primary school level.

mains_linkage.question: Critically evaluate the impact of Wood's Despatch of 1854 on the institutionalization of modern education in India.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Grants-in-aid was introduced and universities were recommended. Statement 3 is false because vernaculars were promoted at lower levels.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the nuanced tiered language policy established by Charles Wood in 1854.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Primary = vernacular; High school = Anglo-vernacular; University = English. Eliminate 'all levels'.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement 3, which is false due to the 'all levels' extreme claim.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes candidates believe British colonialists mandated English from primary school upwards.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Wood's Despatch explicitly insisted on vernacular primary schooling.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement 3 while omitting university creation (Calcutta, Bombay, Madras universities were established in 1857 based directly on it).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Reverses correct and incorrect statements.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Universities were definitely recommended.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Fails to spot the extreme qualifier 'at all levels' in Statement 3.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Common trap for students who broadly associate Wood's Despatch with English promotion.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Always eliminate universal language medium claims.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Parliament - Committees on Subordinate Legislation & Delegated Law
question_text: With reference to the Parliament of India, which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, by-laws etc. conferred by the constitution of delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation ?
explanation:
The Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations, rules, sub-rules, and bye-laws delegated by Parliament or conferred by the Constitution are being properly exercised within the limits of such delegation.
Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have their own Committee on Subordinate Legislation (constituted in 1953 in Lok Sabha), consisting of 15 members in each House.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: Parliamentary Committees - Committees to Inquire and Scrutinize)
elimination_trap: Candidates often confuse the Committee on Subordinate Legislation with the Rules Committee or Committee on Government Assurances.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the concept of delegated legislation and evaluate the effectiveness of the Committee on Subordinate Legislation in checking executive excesses.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Committee on Government Assurances examines assurances, promises, and undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests scrutiny committees vs legislative delegation committees.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Assurances committee tracks promises made by ministers, not statutory rules.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation scrutinizes whether executive rule-making stays within the statutory limits of delegated legislation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Directly matches the constitutional/procedural definition of subordinate legislation scrutiny.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Delegated rule-making = Subordinate legislation.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Rules Committee considers matters of procedure and conduct of business in the House itself, not executive delegated rules.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plays on the word 'rules'.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Rules Committee governs House procedures, not external executive bye-laws.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Business Advisory Committee allocates time for the discussion of government legislative and other business brought before the House.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Presents another prominent parliamentary committee.
option_analysis.mental_filter: BAC sets the parliamentary timetable.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Social Justice & Education - Right to Education Act & NCTE
question_text:
Consider the following statements: 
•  As per the Right to Education (RTE) Act, to be eligible for appointment as a teacher in a State, a person would be required to possess the minimum qualiﬁcation laid down by the concerned State Council of Teacher Education. 
•  As per the RTE Act, for teaching primary classes, a candidate is required to pass a Teacher Eligibility Test conducted in accordance with the National Council of Teacher Education guidelines. 
•  In India, more than 90% of teacher education institutions are directly under the State Governments. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Section 23(1) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, the minimum qualifications for appointment as a teacher are laid down by an academic authority authorized by the Central Government, which is the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), NOT the concerned State Council.
2. Statement 2 is correct: Under NCTE guidelines issued pursuant to the RTE Act, passing a Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) is mandatory for appointment as a teacher in classes I to VIII (primary and upper primary).
3. Statement 3 is incorrect: In India, the vast majority (over 90%) of teacher education institutions (TEIs offering B.Ed./D.El.Ed.) are in the private sector, NOT directly under the State Governments.
standard_book_ref: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009; NCTE Regulations; Justice Verma Commission on Teacher Education
elimination_trap: Aspirants assume education is a State subject and think State Councils determine qualifications, forgetting RTE Act relies on the central NCTE.

mains_linkage.question: Analyze the governance bottlenecks in teacher education institutions in India and suggest reforms to improve foundational learning outcomes under the RTE Act.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is false because NCTE (a central authority) sets teacher qualifications, not State Councils.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits confusion over federal jurisdiction in school education regulation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Section 23 of RTE Act designates NCTE as the sole apex qualification authority.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is correct (TET is mandatory under NCTE guidelines for primary teaching). Statements 1 and 3 are factually incorrect.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests exact knowledge of national teacher eligibility norms.
option_analysis.mental_filter: TET is a national statutory prerequisite under RTE guidelines.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both Statements 1 and 3 are completely incorrect.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Lures candidates unaware of the massive commercial privatization of teacher training colleges in India.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Over 90% of teacher training institutes are private colleges.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 3 is factually inverted (the private sector accounts for >90% of TEIs).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Inverts public vs private sector share in higher education.
option_analysis.mental_filter: State governments run only a tiny minority of teacher training colleges.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Indian Culture - Festivals, Performing Arts & Martial Traditions
question_text:
Consider the following pairs: 
              Tradition State                         State  
•  Chapchar Kut festival                Mizoram 
•  Khonom Parba ballad                Manipur 
•  Thang-Ta dance                         Sikkim 
 Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Pair 1 is correctly matched: Chapchar Kut is the most significant spring festival of Mizoram, celebrated in March after clearing the forest for Jhum (slash-and-burn) cultivation.
2. Pair 2 is correctly matched: Khongjom Parba is a traditional musical ballad singing style of Manipur, depicting the heroic defense of the Manipuris against the British in the 1891 Anglo-Manipur Battle of Khongjom.
3. Pair 3 is incorrectly matched: Thang-Ta (Huyen Langlon) is the ancient traditional martial art and dance form of Manipur (not Sikkim), involving sword (Thang) and spear (Ta).
standard_book_ref: Nitin Singhania - Indian Art and Culture (Chapters: Fairs and Festivals & Martial Arts of India); Sangeet Natak Akademi Publications
elimination_trap: Candidates often mistake Thang-Ta as Himalayan/Tibetan and attribute it to Sikkim, whereas it is the celebrated martial art of the Meiteis of Manipur.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the rich diversity of traditional folk performing arts and martial traditions in Northeast India, highlighting their cultural resilience.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Khongjom Parba, which is indisputably an authentic Manipuri ballad.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubts Manipuri ballad tradition.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Khongjom Parba honors the 1891 battle fought in Manipur.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Thang-Ta belongs to Manipur, making Pair 3 incorrect.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests cultural knowledge of Northeast traditions across states.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Thang-Ta is Manipuri martial arts. Eliminating Pair 3 leaves Option B.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Pair 3 is completely mismatched (Thang-Ta is from Manipur, not Sikkim).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Capitalizes on vague geographical association of Northeast martial dances.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Thang-Ta = Manipur.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes incorrect Pair 3.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Catches candidates who know Khongjom Parba but fail to spot the Sikkim mismatch.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Thang-Ta cannot be from Sikkim.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Statutory & Regulatory Bodies - FSSAI & Food Safety Legislation
question_text:
Consider the following statements: 
•  The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 replaced the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. 
•  The Food Safety and Standard Authority of India (FSSAI) is under the charge of Director General of Health Services in the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is correct: The Food Safety and Standards Act (FSSA), 2006 consolidated various food-related laws and repealed older fragmented statutes, including the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, Fruit Products Order, 1955, and Meat Food Products Order, 1973.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is an autonomous statutory body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is headed by a non-executive Chairperson appointed by the Central Government (in the rank of Secretary to Government of India) and an executive CEO. It is NOT under the charge of the Director General of Health Services (DGHS).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: Statutory Bodies); Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
elimination_trap: DGHS is a technical directorate under MoHFW, whereas FSSAI was specifically constituted as an independent statutory authority outside DGHS control.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the institutional capacity and regulatory challenges of FSSAI in enforcing food safety standards and curbing adulteration in India.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is correct (replaced 1954 PFA Act) and Statement 2 is incorrect (FSSAI is autonomous with its own Chairperson/CEO, not under DGHS).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests statutory consolidation of food laws and administrative hierarchy of regulatory bodies.
option_analysis.mental_filter: FSSAI has an autonomous Chairperson/CEO, not subordinate to DGHS.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is administrative disinformation; DGHS heads medical services, not the autonomous food safety authority.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Confuses DGHS with FSSAI leadership.
option_analysis.mental_filter: FSSAI is an independent statutory authority.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrectly accepts Statement 2.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Common trap for candidates who know FSSAI falls under MoHFW but do not know its internal leadership structure.
option_analysis.mental_filter: FSSAI reports directly to the Ministry, not via DGHS.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is the cardinal purpose for which the FSS Act 2006 was passed.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubting the repeal of older food adulteration legislation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: FSSA 2006 expressly consolidated and replaced the 1954 Act.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: International Relations - West Asia & Middle East Peace Process
question_text: The term  “two-state solution"  is sometimes mentioned in the news in the context of the affairs of
explanation:
The 'two-state solution' is the primary framework proposed for resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
It envisions an independent State of Palestine living peacefully side by side with the State of Israel, based on pre-1967 borders with mutually agreed land swaps, having mutually recognized capitals (Jerusalem) and security arrangements.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII - Contemporary World Politics; Ministry of External Affairs Briefs on West Asia Policy
elimination_trap: Two-state solution is frequently mentioned in international news concerning West Asia, making it an unmissable high-yield foreign policy term.

mains_linkage.question: Critically evaluate India's de-hyphenated foreign policy toward Israel and Palestine in the context of the two-state solution.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: China operates under the 'One Country, Two Systems' framework regarding Hong Kong and Taiwan, not 'two-state solution'.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plays on terminological resemblance with China's 'Two Systems'.
option_analysis.mental_filter: China is 'One Country, Two Systems', not 'two-state solution'.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: The two-state solution is the universally acknowledged diplomatic formula for peace between Israel and Palestine.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Direct identification of a major international diplomatic framework.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Two-state solution = Israel-Palestine peace process.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Iraq's internal political challenges involve federalism with Iraqi Kurdistan, not a 'two-state solution'.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Distractor from Middle Eastern conflicts.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Iraq is a single federal republic.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Yemen suffers from a civil conflict between Houthi rebels and the internationally recognized government.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Another ongoing Arabian Peninsula conflict used as a distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Yemen conflict is sectarian/civil, not two-state.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Welfare Legislation - National Food Security Act, 2013
question_text:
With reference to the provisions made under the National Food Security Act, 2013, consider the following statements: 
•  The families coming under the category of ‘below poverty line (BPL)' only are eligible to receive subsidised food grains.  
•  The eldest woman in a household, of age 18 years or above, shall be the head of the household for the purpose of issuance of a ration card.  
•  Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a ‘take-home ration’ of 1600 calories per day during pregnancy and for six months thereafter. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013:
1. Statement 1 is incorrect: Coverage under NFSA is not limited to BPL families only. It covers up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population, categorizing beneficiaries into Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Households (PHH), moving away from traditional BPL targeting.
2. Statement 2 is correct: Under Section 13(1) of the NFSA, the eldest woman who is not less than eighteen years of age in every eligible household shall be head of the household for the purpose of issue of ration cards (a key women-empowerment feature).
3. Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Section 4, pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a meal free of charge (satisfying nutritional norms of 600 calories and 18-20g protein, NOT 1600 calories) and maternity benefit of not less than Rs. 6,000.
standard_book_ref: The National Food Security Act, 2013; Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution Guidelines
elimination_trap: Statement 3 inflates the supplementary calorie intake to an absurd 1600 calories per day (normal supplementary entitlement is 600 kcal), and Statement 1 wrongly uses 'BPL only'.

mains_linkage.question: Examine how the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013 transformed the welfare paradigm in India from a charity-based model to a rights-based entitlement.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is false because NFSA covers 67% of India's population under Priority and Antyodaya categories, not just BPL.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the fundamental shift from Targeted PDS (BPL/APL) to NFSA entitlements.
option_analysis.mental_filter: NFSA covers two-thirds of the total population, far broader than BPL.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is correct. The eldest woman (18+ years) is statutory head of household for the issuance of ration cards.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Highlights the landmark gender-empowerment mandate embedded in food security legislation.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Section 13 explicitly recognizes the eldest woman (18+) as the head of household.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 3 exaggerates calorie norms (600 kcal is provided, not 1600 kcal).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Numerical exaggeration trap.
option_analysis.mental_filter: 1600 calories is almost an entire day's caloric requirement, not a supplementary take-home ration.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 3 is scientifically and legally inaccurate regarding supplementary nutrition norms.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Catches candidates who do not recall dietary calorie guidelines.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Supplementary norm under Schedule II of NFSA is 600 calories.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Intellectual Property Rights - Geographical Indications & TRIPS
question_text: India enacted  The Geographical Indications of Goods  (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 in order to comply with the obligations to
explanation:
India enacted 'The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999' to comply with its obligations under the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS).
Articles 22 to 24 of the TRIPS Agreement mandate the protection of geographical indications to prevent misleading the public regarding the geographical origin of goods and to prevent unfair competition.
standard_book_ref: Ramesh Singh - Indian Economy (Chapter: International Economic Organizations - WTO & TRIPS); IPR Laws in India
elimination_trap: Aspirants might confuse UNCTAD or ILO with trade-related intellectual property obligations, but TRIPS is administered exclusively by the WTO.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the role of the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 in promoting rural livelihoods and protecting traditional indigenous craftsmanship under WTO norms.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: ILO governs international labour standards and employment conventions, not intellectual property.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Presents a specialized UN agency as a distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: ILO regulates workers' rights, not product origin tags.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: IMF deals with macroeconomic surveillance, balance of payments, and financial stability, not IP law.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Bretton Woods distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: IMF provides balance of payments financing, not intellectual property rules.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: UNCTAD focuses on development dimensions of trade, but binding intellectual property obligations are created by WTO TRIPS.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Trades on UN trade body association.
option_analysis.mental_filter: TRIPS Agreement is under the WTO.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: The GI Act 1999 was enacted to meet India's obligations under the WTO's TRIPS Agreement.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard statutory-treaty linkage question.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Geographical Indications = WTO TRIPS Agreement.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Mineral Resources & Mining Law - State Jurisdiction & Distribution
question_text:
Consider the following statements: 
•  In India, State Governments do not have the power to auction non-coal mines. 
•  Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand do not have gold mines. 
•  Rajasthan has iron ore mines. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is incorrect: Under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2015, State Governments are specifically empowered to grant mineral concessions through competitive e-auction for both major and minor minerals, including non-coal mines.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: Both Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand have known gold deposits and mining activities. In Andhra Pradesh, Ramagiri (Anantapur) and Jonnagiri (Kurnool) host gold deposits. In Jharkhand, alluvial gold is panned along the Subarnarekha River and gold deposits exist in Kunderkocha (East Singhbhum).
3. Statement 3 is correct: Rajasthan has significant iron ore reserves located in Jaipur (Morija-Banol), Udaipur (Nathra-ki-Pal), Jhunjhunu (Dabla), and Sikar districts.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XII - India: People and Economy (Chapter 7: Mineral and Energy Resources); Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) Year Book
elimination_trap: Statements 1 and 2 use the absolute negative 'do not have', which is easily falsified since states conduct mineral auctions and gold occurs in AP and Jharkhand.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the geographical distribution of major metallic mineral resources in India, with special reference to peninsular and extra-peninsular shields.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement 1 and 2, both of which are false negative statements.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Combines two absolute negative claims.
option_analysis.mental_filter: States auction non-coal mines and Subarnarekha (Jharkhand) means 'streak of gold'.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand have prominent gold occurrences.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes candidates only know Kolar and Hutti in Karnataka.
option_analysis.mental_filter: While Karnataka leads, AP and Jharkhand also have documented gold mines.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Accepts Statement 1, disregarding the MMDR Amendment Act 2015 auction framework.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests mineral law reforms of 2015.
option_analysis.mental_filter: State governments hold ownership of minerals within their borders and conduct auctions.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 3 only is correct. Rajasthan possesses active iron ore deposits (Morija-Banol, Nathra-ki-Pal).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests precise economic geography of metallic deposits.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Eliminating Statements 1 and 2 immediately leaves Option D.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Digital Financial Architecture - BHIM UPI Authentication
question_text:
With reference to digital payments, consider the following statements: 
•  BHIM app allows the user to transfer money to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account. 
•  While a chip-pin debit card has four factors authentication, BHIM app has only two factors of authentication. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is correct: Bharat Interface for Money (BHIM) allows users to transfer funds instantly to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account using a Virtual Payment Address (VPA), mobile number, or Account/IFSC.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: Both chip-and-PIN debit cards and the BHIM app utilize two-factor authentication (2FA). A chip-and-PIN debit card uses 'something you have' (the physical card chip) and 'something you know' (the 4-digit PIN), which is two factors, NOT four factors. BHIM also relies on two factors: the registered mobile device binding/SIM card (device fingerprint) and the UPI PIN.
standard_book_ref: RBI Guidelines on Digital Payment Authentication; NPCI BHIM UPI Architectural Whitepaper
elimination_trap: Statement 2 invents an imaginary 'four factors authentication' for debit cards, whereas international cybersecurity standards universally implement two-factor authentication (2FA).

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the security and scalability of the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) as an open-protocol digital payments public good.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is correct (BHIM permits interoperable fund transfer to any UPI bank), and Statement 2 is false (chip-and-pin uses 2 factors, not 4).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests cybersecurity authentication primitives (factors of authentication).
option_analysis.mental_filter: Authentication factors are: something you know (PIN), something you have (card/phone), something you are (biometrics). Chip+PIN = 2 factors.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 falsely claims four factors of authentication for standard chip-and-PIN cards.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Fabricates higher-order authentication factors.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Commercial debit cards use 2FA, never 4FA.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Accepts the erroneous 'four factors' assertion in Statement 2.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Lures candidates unaware of multi-factor authentication taxonomy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Eliminate Statement 2 for technical absurdity.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is the defining core functionality of the BHIM app.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Over-skeptical trap on UPI interoperability.
option_analysis.mental_filter: BHIM transfers money seamlessly across all UPI-member banks.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Indian Geography - Latitudinal and Longitudinal Coordinates
question_text: Among the following cities, which one lies on   a longitude closest to that of Delhi?
explanation:
Coordinates of Delhi and the given cities:
- Delhi: ~77° 12' E longitude (28° 36' N)
- Bengaluru: ~77° 35' E longitude (difference ~0° 23' E) -> Closest to Delhi's meridian
- Hyderabad: ~78° 28' E longitude (difference ~1° 16' E)
- Nagpur: ~79° 05' E longitude (difference ~1° 53' E)
- Pune: ~73° 51' E longitude (difference ~3° 21' W)
Bengaluru lies almost due south of Delhi along virtually the same meridian (~77° E).
standard_book_ref: Oxford School Atlas; NCERT Class XI - India: Physical Environment
elimination_trap: Many candidates assume Nagpur is closest to Delhi's longitude because it is located in the geographical center of India (Zero Mile Stone), but Nagpur is around 79° E, whereas Delhi and Bengaluru both align near 77° E.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the spatial distribution of major metropolitan urban agglomerations along India's north-south meridian axis.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Bengaluru (~77° 35' E) is longitudinal twin to Delhi (~77° 12' E), differing by less than half a degree.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Classic UPSC map-based coordinate awareness question.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Draw a straight vertical line south from Delhi on India's map: it passes right through Bengaluru.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Hyderabad lies further east at ~78° 28' E.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Presents a Deccan city that seems centrally aligned.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Hyderabad is more than 1° east of Delhi.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Nagpur is at ~79° 05' E (nearly 2 degrees east of Delhi).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits Nagpur's reputation as the geographical center ('Zero Mile') of India.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Nagpur's longitude is 79° E, while Delhi is 77° E.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Pune lies far to the west at ~73° 51' E.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Western Indian distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Pune is over 3 degrees west of Delhi.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: Labour Conventions & Social Justice - International Labour Organization
question_text: International Labour Organization’s   Conventions 138 and 182 are related to
options: Adaptation of agriculture practices to global climate change
Regulation of food prices and food security
explanation:
International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions 138 and 182 are the fundamental conventions concerning child labour:
- Convention 138: Minimum Age Convention, 1973 (stipulating that the minimum age for employment shall not be less than the age of completion of compulsory schooling, generally 15 years).
- Convention 182: Worst Forms of Child Labour Convention, 1999 (calling for the immediate prohibition and elimination of the worst forms of child labour, including slavery, trafficking, and hazardous work).
India ratified both core Conventions 138 and 182 in June 2017.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Labour and Employment Annual Report 2017-18; ILO Fundamental Conventions Overview
elimination_trap: Aspirants who miss the 2017 ratification news might guess gender parity or agriculture, but 138 and 182 are globally famous child labour instruments.

mains_linkage.question: Assess the legal and institutional impact of India ratifying ILO Conventions 138 and 182 on child protection and child labour abolition.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Conventions 138 (Minimum Age) and 182 (Worst Forms) relate directly to child labour eradication.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Directly tests India's high-profile 2017 ratification of core ILO conventions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: ILO 138 + 182 = Child Labour.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: ILO conventions do not address agricultural climate change adaptation.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Environmental distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: ILO deals with labour standards, not agricultural climate adaptation.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Food security and price regulation fall under FAO, WTO, and WFP mandates.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Commodity trade distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Food price regulation is outside ILO purview.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Gender parity in employment is covered under ILO Convention 100 (Equal Remuneration) and 111 (Discrimination).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Presents other core ILO conventions as plausible alternatives.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Gender parity = Conventions 100 and 111; Child labour = 138 and 182.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Parliament - Financial Legislation & Money Bill Definition
question_text: Regarding Money Bill , which of the following statements is   not   correct?
options: A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of money out of the Contingency Fund of India.
A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
explanation:
Under Article 110 of the Constitution of India, a Money Bill deals with:
1. The imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of any tax.
2. The regulation of borrowing of money or giving of guarantees by the Government of India.
3. The custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India, the payment of moneys into or withdrawal of moneys from any such fund.
4. The appropriation of moneys out of the CONSOLIDATED Fund of India (Article 110(1)(d)).
Statement C is NOT correct because appropriation of money occurs out of the Consolidated Fund of India, NOT the Contingency Fund of India. Advances from the Contingency Fund are made by the President under Article 267 to meet unforeseen expenditure, pending authorization by Parliament.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: Parliament - Money Bills); Constitution of India (Article 110)
elimination_trap: Aspirants miss the subtle distinction between the 'Consolidated Fund of India' (which requires statutory appropriation under Article 114) and the 'Contingency Fund of India' (which provides executive advances).

mains_linkage.question: Examine the constitutional definition and procedural safeguards regarding Money Bills under Article 110, in the light of controversies over Rajya Sabha bypassing.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: This is a verbatim correct statement under Article 110(1)(a).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard tax clause under Money Bill definition.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Tax measures are core Money Bill provisions.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: This is a verbatim correct statement under Article 110(1)(c).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Custody of both funds is part of Article 110.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Custody is covered under Article 110(1)(c).

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement C is NOT correct. Money bills appropriate money out of the Consolidated Fund of India (Article 110(1)(d)), not the Contingency Fund.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Substitutes Contingency Fund for Consolidated Fund in the appropriation clause.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Appropriation is strictly out of the Consolidated Fund of India.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: This is a verbatim correct statement under Article 110(1)(b).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Government borrowing regulation is explicitly part of Article 110.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Borrowing regulation is a Money Bill matter.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Union Executive - Presidential Election System & Vote Values
question_text:
With reference to the  election of the President of India , consider the following statements:
• The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State.
• The value of the vote of MPs of the Loksabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajyasabha
Which of the following statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
Under Article 55 of the Constitution of India (Manner of election of President):
1. Statement 1 is correct: The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State because it is calculated based on the population of the State divided by the total number of elected members in the State Legislative Assembly (multiplied by 1/1000). For example, in the 2017 election, an MLA's vote value was highest in Uttar Pradesh (208) and lowest in Sikkim (7).
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: The value of the vote of every elected MP (whether from Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) is identical and equal. The value of an MP's vote is calculated by dividing the total value of votes of all elected MLAs across all States by the total number of elected MPs of both Houses of Parliament (776 MPs).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: President - Election of the President)
elimination_trap: Aspirants assume Lok Sabha MPs have higher vote value because Lok Sabha has larger democratic representation, forgetting all MPs share an identical formula.

mains_linkage.question: Explain the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote in the election of the President of India, highlighting the principle of federal uniformity.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is correct (MLA vote value varies by state population) and Statement 2 is incorrect (all MPs have equal vote value).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the mathematical mechanics of parity between the Union and the States under Article 55.
option_analysis.mental_filter: MLA vote values reflect state populations; MP vote values are identical across LS and RS.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is false because both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs have the exact same vote value (708 in 2017).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Preys on the intuition that Lok Sabha is the 'popular' house.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The formula divides total state votes by total elected MPs of BOTH houses equally.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Fails to spot the error in Statement 2 regarding inter-house equality.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Lures candidates unaware of parity between parliamentary chambers in presidential elections.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Article 55 guarantees equality among all elected members of Parliament.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is an undeniable constitutional fact (e.g. UP MLA = 208, Sikkim MLA = 7).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Over-skeptical trap on state population variations.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Population variation directly drives MLA vote values.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Nuclear Energy - IAEA Additional Protocol Implications
question_text: In the Indian context, what is the implication of ratifying the ‘Additional Protocol' with the ‘International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)'?
options: The civilian nuclear reactors come under IAEA safeguards.
The military nuclear installations come under the inspection of IAEA
The country will have the privilege to buy uranium from the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).
The country automatically becomes a member of the NSG.
explanation:
In the Indian context, ratifying the 'Additional Protocol' with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) means:
1. Civilian nuclear facilities/reactors that India voluntarily placed under IAEA safeguards (following the India-Specific Safeguards Agreement in 2008) are subject to expanded monitoring and verification by the IAEA.
2. Military nuclear installations remain strictly outside IAEA safeguards and inspections under India's separation plan.
3. Ratifying the Additional Protocol does NOT automatically grant NSG membership or provide an automatic privilege to buy uranium (which depends on bilateral civil nuclear agreements under the 2008 NSG waiver).
standard_book_ref: Rajiv Sikri - Challenge and Strategy; Ministry of External Affairs Bilateral Nuclear Cooperation Briefs
elimination_trap: Options C and D use 'privilege to buy' and 'automatically becomes a member', both of which are common misconceptions about export regime access.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the strategic significance of the separation of civilian and military nuclear facilities in India's nuclear diplomacy and IAEA engagement.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: The Additional Protocol places designated civilian nuclear reactors under enhanced IAEA safeguards and inspections.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Directly tests the functional legal outcome of India's 2014 ratification of the IAEA Additional Protocol.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Additional Protocol = Enhanced IAEA safeguards on civilian reactors only.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Military nuclear installations are totally excluded from IAEA inspection under India's separation plan.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Extreme claim that violates India's strategic nuclear autonomy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: India never placed military reactors under international inspection.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Uranium purchase is governed by bilateral inter-governmental agreements under the 2008 NSG waiver, not simply the IAEA protocol.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Conflates IAEA safeguards with commercial supply contracts.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Safeguards are a prerequisite, but do not create an automatic purchase privilege.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: NSG membership requires full consensus of all 48 members; IAEA safeguards do not confer membership.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plays on the frequent association between IAEA protocols and NSG admission.
option_analysis.mental_filter: NSG membership is blocked by geopolitical consensus, not IAEA protocol ratification.

subject: Economy
sub_topic: International Trade - ASEAN Free Trade Agreements
question_text:
Consider the following countries :
1. Australia
2. Canada
3. China
4. India
5. Japan
6. USA
Which of the above are among the ‘free-trade partners' of ASEAN ?
explanation:
ASEAN has free-trade agreements (FTAs) with six external partners (known as ASEAN+6 or the original RCEP negotiating partners):
1. Australia (AANZFTA)
2. China (ACFTA)
3. India (AIFTA)
4. Japan (AJCEP)
5. Republic of Korea (AKFTA)
6. New Zealand (AANZFTA)
Canada and the USA do NOT have a free-trade agreement with ASEAN (trade discussions with Canada started much later, and the US has a Trade and Investment Framework Arrangement, not an FTA). Thus, from the given list, 1 (Australia), 3 (China), 4 (India), and 5 (Japan) are free-trade partners.
standard_book_ref: Economic Survey (Chapter: International Trade); ASEAN Secretariat Official Portal
elimination_trap: Canada and the USA are major economic powers, but neither is part of ASEAN's existing free-trade partner network. Eliminating 2 (Canada) and 6 (USA) immediately gives Option C.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate India's trade trajectory with ASEAN under the ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement (AIFTA) and discuss concerns regarding trade deficits.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Canada (2), which does not have an operational FTA with ASEAN.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests knowledge of ASEAN+6 trade agreements.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Canada is not an ASEAN FTA partner.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes USA (6), which has never signed an FTA with the ASEAN bloc.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes candidates consider the US an FTA partner due to massive trade volume.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The US does not have an FTA with ASEAN.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Australia, China, India, and Japan (1, 3, 4, 5) are all free-trade partners of ASEAN.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard regional trade bloc partner question.
option_analysis.mental_filter: ASEAN's 6 FTA partners: China, Japan, Korea, India, Australia, NZ. Eliminate Canada and USA.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes both Canada (2) and USA (6).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Western hemisphere distractor bundle.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Neither North American nation is an ASEAN FTA partner.

subject: Environment & Ecology
sub_topic: Climate Change Initiatives - Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture
question_text:
With reference to the ‘Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA)', which of the following statements is/are correct ?
1. GACSA is an outcome of the Climate Summit held in Paris in 2015.
2. Membership of GACSA does not create any binding obligations.
3. India was instrumental in the creation of GACSA.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is incorrect: The Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA) was launched at the UN Climate Summit held in New York in September 2014, NOT at the Paris Climate Summit (COP21) in 2015.
2. Statement 2 is correct: Membership of GACSA is entirely voluntary and does NOT create any binding legal obligations on its member governments or institutions.
3. Statement 3 is incorrect: India was NOT instrumental in the creation of GACSA and is not a member country of GACSA, as India expressed serious reservations that agriculture should not be subjected to binding mitigation targets under climate frameworks.
standard_book_ref: FAO Portal on Climate-Smart Agriculture; Down to Earth Environment Annual Analysis
elimination_trap: Aspirants assume India champions all global agricultural alliances, but India explicitly avoided joining GACSA over fears of climate emission obligations on smallholders.

mains_linkage.question: Examine India's stance on incorporating agriculture into global carbon emission mitigation negotiations under the UNFCCC.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 gives the wrong summit (2014 New York, not 2015 Paris) and Statement 3 falsely claims India founded it.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs two common historical-diplomatic assumptions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: GACSA was 2014 New York; India refused to join.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 only is correct. GACSA is a voluntary multi-stakeholder alliance without binding obligations.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests the voluntary vs legally binding nature of international climate alliances.
option_analysis.mental_filter: GACSA is purely voluntary/non-binding. India is not a member.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement 3, which is false because India deliberately stayed out of GACSA.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits the assumption that India participates in all agricultural climate platforms.
option_analysis.mental_filter: India stayed away from GACSA due to concerns about corporate agriculture.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Accepts all statements uncritically.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-of-the-above trap on global climate initiatives.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Check founding year (2014) and India's membership status.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: E-Governance & ICT - Digital India Mission Architecture
question_text:
Which of the following is/are the aim/aims of "Digital India" Plan of the Government of India ?
1. Formation of India's own Internet companies like China did.
2. Establish a policy framework to encourage overseas multinational corporations that collect Big Data to build their large data centres within our national geographical boundaries.
3. Connect many of our villages to the Internet and bring Wi-Fi to many of our schools, public places and major tourist centres.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
explanation:
With reference to the 'Digital India' program launched in 2015:
1. Statement 1 is incorrect: The formation of state-controlled Indian internet companies (like China's Baidu or Alibaba behind the Great Firewall) is NOT an aim of Digital India. India promotes an open, democratic internet and fosters domestic startups through market competition.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: The aim is not to formulate policies to coerce overseas MNCs to build large data centers in India; policy focuses on domestic digital infrastructure, local entrepreneurship, and data sovereignty.
3. Statement 3 is correct: A core pillar of Digital India is broadband highways and universal access to mobile connectivity—connecting 2.5 lakh gram panchayats through BharatNet, and providing public Wi-Fi in schools, major tourist hubs, and public spaces.
standard_book_ref: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) - Digital India Pillars; NITI Aayog Strategy for New India
elimination_trap: Statements 1 and 2 sound like protectionist industrial policy, whereas Digital India is fundamentally an infrastructure and e-governance delivery initiative.

mains_linkage.question: Evaluate the achievements of the Digital India programme in bridging the digital divide and promoting citizen-centric e-governance.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statements 1 and 2 represent authoritarian protectionist policies, not the stated pillars of Digital India.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Attributes China's internet ecosystem model to democratic India.
option_analysis.mental_filter: India does not pursue the Chinese state-controlled internet model.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 3 only is correct. Digital India aims to connect villages (BharatNet) and establish public Wi-Fi access.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Accurately identifies the foundational digital infrastructure pillar of the program.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Broadband for all villages and public Wi-Fi are official Digital India pillars.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Includes Statement 2, which misinterprets data center policy as a primary program objective.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Distorts data localization discussions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Data center policies are separate from Digital India's citizen-facing goals.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Accepts extreme policy statements 1 and 2.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: All-inclusive trap.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Statements 1 and 2 are completely unaligned with official government documents.

subject: Geography
sub_topic: Places in News - West Asia Geopolitical Locations
question_text:
Consider the following pairs :
Towns sometimes mentioned in news                Country
1. Aleppo                                                             Syria
2. Kirkuk                                                              Yemen
3. Mosul                                                               Palestine
4. Mazar-i-sharif                                                 Afghanistan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explanation:
Geographical locations of the towns in news:
1. Aleppo: A major historic city in northern Syria, heavily featured during the Syrian Civil War (Correct).
2. Kirkuk: A major oil-rich city located in northern Iraq (incorrectly matched with Yemen).
3. Mosul: The second-largest city of Iraq, located along the Tigris River, famous for the battle against ISIS (incorrectly matched with Palestine).
4. Mazar-i-sharif: The fourth-largest city of Afghanistan, capital of Balkh province (Correct).
Therefore, pairs 1 and 4 are correctly matched.
standard_book_ref: Oxford School Atlas; Contemporary International News Compilations
elimination_trap: Kirkuk and Mosul are both in Iraq. Aspirants who know Mosul is Iraqi can immediately eliminate pairs 2 and 3.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the geopolitical significance of strategic urban centers in West Asia in shaping contemporary regional security dynamics.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Kirkuk is in Iraq, not Yemen.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Mismatches an Iraqi city with Yemen.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Kirkuk is the center of Iraq's northern oilfields.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Pairs 1 and 4 are correctly matched (Aleppo in Syria, Mazar-i-sharif in Afghanistan).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs widely reported conflict zones in international news.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Aleppo = Syria; Mazar-i-sharif = Afghanistan.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both Kirkuk (Yemen) and Mosul (Palestine) are falsely matched; both belong to Iraq.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pairs two Iraqi cities matched to wrong countries.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Both Kirkuk and Mosul are situated in Iraq.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Mosul is in Iraq, not Palestine.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Relies on vague Middle Eastern conflict associations.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Mosul is the famous Iraqi city on the Tigris.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Constitutional Development - Government of India Act 1935
question_text: In the Federation established by  The Government of India Act of 1935 , residuary powers were given to the
explanation:
The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation and divided legislative powers into three lists:
1. Federal Legislative List (for Federal Legislature)
2. Provincial Legislative List (for Provincial Legislatures)
3. Concurrent Legislative List (for both)
Residuary legislative powers were NOT allocated to either the Federal or the Provincial Legislature; instead, under Section 104, residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General to allocate in his discretion to either legislature.
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: Historical Background); Bipan Chandra - Modern India
elimination_trap: Aspirants confuse the 1935 Act with the modern Indian Constitution, where Article 248 vests residuary powers in the Union Parliament (Federal Legislature).

mains_linkage.question: Compare the scheme of division of legislative powers under the Government of India Act, 1935 with the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: In the modern Indian Constitution (Article 248), residuary powers lie with Parliament, but in the 1935 Act they lay with the Governor General.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Anachronistic trap confusing 1935 colonial federation with 1950 republican Constitution.
option_analysis.mental_filter: In the 1935 Act, the Governor-General exercised residuary powers in his discretion.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Residuary powers were vested in the Governor-General under the 1935 Act.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard constitutional history question on colonial federalism.
option_analysis.mental_filter: 1935 Act residuary powers = Governor-General.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Provincial Legislatures had jurisdiction only over the Provincial List.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests US-style state residuary power misconceptions.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Provincial legislatures were not granted residuary powers.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Provincial Governors had executive powers within provinces, but residuary legislative assignment was the prerogative of the Governor-General.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Confuses Governor-General with Provincial Governors.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Governor-General held the apex discretionary authority.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: State Legislature - Office of the Speaker Vacation & Dissolution
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
1. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
2. Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately. Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
explanation:
Under Article 179 of the Constitution of India (Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker):
1. Statement 1 is correct: Article 179(a) provides that a member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker of an Assembly shall vacate his office if he ceases to be a member of the Assembly.
2. Statement 2 is incorrect: The proviso to Article 179 states that whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved, the Speaker shall NOT vacate his office immediately, but shall continue in office until immediately before the first meeting of the Assembly after the dissolution (to maintain institutional continuity).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: State Legislature - Presiding Officers)
elimination_trap: Aspirants assume dissolution dissolves everything immediately, forgetting the Speaker remains in office until the new Assembly meets.

mains_linkage.question: Examine the constitutional role of the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly and evaluate mechanisms to ensure neutrality of the office.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is correct (losing seat vacates Speaker's office) and Statement 2 is false (Speaker does not vacate immediately upon dissolution).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests precise knowledge of constitutional provisos ensuring institutional continuity.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Speaker remains in office during dissolution until the next House convenes.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 2 is directly contradicted by the explicit proviso to Article 179.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Plays on the extreme word 'immediately'.
option_analysis.mental_filter: The Speaker never vacates 'immediately' on dissolution.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Incorrectly accepts Statement 2.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Traps candidates who do not know the constitutional mechanism for legislative transition.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Administrative gap is prevented by keeping the Speaker in office.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Statement 1 is an explicit, mandatory constitutional rule under Article 179(a).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubting membership qualification requirement.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Only an active member can hold the office of Speaker.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: Political Theory - Concepts of Liberty, Rights & Law
question_text: Which one of the following reflects the most appropriate relationship between law and liberty ?
options: If there are more laws, there is less liberty.
If there are no laws, there is no liberty.
If there is liberty laws have to be made by the people.
If laws are changed too often, liberty is in danger.
explanation:
The relationship between law and liberty is a foundational theme in political theory:
John Locke famously observed in his Second Treatise of Government: 'Where there is no law, there is no freedom.'
Laws create the predictable, protective framework that prevents arbitrary coercion by stronger individuals, guarantees fundamental rights, and protects personal autonomy. Without law, there is anarchy and the rule of might, extinguishing genuine liberty.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI - Political Theory (Chapter 2: Freedom / Liberty); O.P. Gauba - An Introduction to Political Theory
elimination_trap: Candidates often pick Option A ('more laws, less liberty'), which reflects a negative classical libertarian caricature rather than the balanced political philosophy tested by UPSC.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the philosophical relationship between the rule of law and individual liberty in a constitutional democracy.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Laws that protect civil rights, prohibit slavery, or enforce equality expand liberty rather than reduce it.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Superficial popular belief that laws are solely restrictive.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Volume of law is not inversely proportional to freedom.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Reflects John Locke's core philosophical premise: without law to protect rights against aggression, liberty cannot exist.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests classical liberal political philosophy.
option_analysis.mental_filter: No law = state of nature/anarchy = no liberty.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: While desirable in a democracy, laws made by monarchs or judicial bodies can also protect fundamental civil liberty.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Conflates democracy with the existential condition for liberty.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Liberty requires the protection of law, regardless of parliamentary vs customary origin.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Touches on legal stability, but does not define the fundamental relationship between law and liberty.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: A secondary prudential observation rather than a core theoretical definition.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Frequent change affects predictability, but does not define liberty's existence.

subject: Polity & Governance
sub_topic: State Executive - Office of the Governor Immunities & Privileges
question_text:
Consider the following statements :
1. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor of a State in any court during his term of office.
2. The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of a State shall not be diminished during his term of office. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation:
1. Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 361(2) and (3) of the Constitution of India, the President or Governor of a State enjoys personal immunity from criminal proceedings during their term of office. No criminal proceedings whatsoever can be instituted or continued in any court, and no process for arrest or imprisonment can be issued.
2. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 158(4) of the Constitution, the emoluments and allowances of the Governor shall not be diminished during his term of office (ensuring constitutional independence).
standard_book_ref: M. Laxmikanth - Indian Polity (Chapter: Governor); Constitution of India (Articles 158 and 361)
elimination_trap: Candidates often confuse criminal immunity (which is absolute during the term) with civil proceedings (which can be initiated after two months' notice for acts done in personal capacity).

mains_linkage.question: Examine the constitutional immunities and discretionary powers of the Governor in India, highlighting areas of federal tension.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Statement 2, which is an explicit constitutional safeguard under Article 158(4).
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Doubts financial protection of high constitutional offices.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Emoluments of Governor, judges, and President cannot be diminished during their term.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Omits Statement 1, disregarding Article 361's absolute criminal immunity.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Assumes criminal immunity cannot be absolute.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Article 361 provides complete criminal immunity during the term of office.

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Both 1 and 2 are correct. Article 361 bars criminal proceedings and Article 158(4) protects emoluments from diminution.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Direct test of constitutional articles safeguarding the Governor's office.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Absolute criminal immunity + protected emoluments = Both 1 and 2.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Rejects two explicit constitutional provisions.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Cynical trap.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Both are verbatim provisions of the Indian Constitution.

subject: History & Culture
sub_topic: Indian Paintings - Rajasthani Schools of Miniature Painting
question_text: The well-known painting "Bani Thani" belongs to the
explanation:
The celebrated painting 'Bani Thani' belongs to the Kishangarh school of Rajasthani miniature painting.
Painted by court master Nihal Chand under the patronage of Raja Sawant Singh (who wrote poetry as Nagari Das), Bani Thani portrays a singer/poetess as Radha with stylized facial features: arched eyebrows, lotus-shaped elongated eyes, a slender neck, and a sharp nose. It is widely acclaimed as the 'Indian Mona Lisa'.
standard_book_ref: NCERT Class XI - An Introduction to Indian Art; Nitin Singhania - Indian Art and Culture (Chapter: Indian Paintings)
elimination_trap: Aspirants might confuse Kishangarh with Bundi or Kangra, but Bani Thani is the single most distinctive masterpiece of the Kishangarh school.

mains_linkage.question: Highlight the distinctive thematic and stylistic features of the Kishangarh school of miniature painting.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Bundi school is renowned for lush vegetation, water bodies, and hunting scenes, not Bani Thani.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Uses another Rajasthani sub-school as a distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Bundi is famous for wildlife and Chhatar Mahal murals.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Jaipur school is characterized by large life-size portraits and Mughal influences, not the stylized Bani Thani.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Dhundhar/Jaipur school distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Jaipur school did not produce the Radha-Bani Thani portrait.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Kangra school is a Pahari painting school of Himachal Pradesh, not a Rajasthani school.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Pahari school distractor.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Kangra is Pahari; Bani Thani is Rajasthani (Kishangarh).

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: Bani Thani was created by Nihal Chand in the Kishangarh school of painting.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Textbook identification of India's most famous miniature painting.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Bani Thani = Nihal Chand = Kishangarh School.

subject: Science & Technology
sub_topic: Defense & Strategic Technology - Ballistic Missile Defense Systems
question_text: What is "Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD)", sometimes seen in the news ?
options: A defence collaboration between Japan and South Korea
explanation:
Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) is an advanced American transportable anti-ballistic missile defense system designed and manufactured by Lockheed Martin for the United States military.
THAAD is engineered to intercept and destroy short-, medium-, and intermediate-range ballistic missiles in their terminal phase (descent or re-entry) using kinetic hit-to-kill technology. It gained widespread global news coverage in 2017-2018 due to its controversial deployment in South Korea to counter North Korean missile threats.
standard_book_ref: Science and Technology Current Affairs; Strategic Defense and Missile Technology Overviews
elimination_trap: Aspirants might guess Israel because of Iron Dome or Arrow, but THAAD is unequivocally an American weapon system.

mains_linkage.question: Discuss the strategic implications of ballistic missile defense systems like THAAD and S-400 on deterrence stability in regional security theaters.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: Israel develops Iron Dome and Arrow, while THAAD is developed and deployed by the United States.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Exploits high visibility of Israeli missile defense technology.
option_analysis.mental_filter: Israel = Iron Dome/David's Sling; THAAD = USA.

option_analysis.label: Trap
option_analysis.diagnosis: India's indigenous program comprises Prithvi Air Defense (PAD) and Advanced Air Defense (AAD), not THAAD.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Tests awareness of DRDO ballistic missile defense nomenclature.
option_analysis.mental_filter: India's BMD is PAD/AAD (Prithvi/Ashwin).

option_analysis.label: ✅ Official UPSC Key
option_analysis.diagnosis: THAAD is an American anti-ballistic missile defense system.
option_analysis.examiner_craft: Standard identification of global military-strategic hardware in news.
